PRINTING THE SCRIPTURES

Extensive preaching

Even if there are delicious and strange dishes available, if you don't taste them, you can't know the taste. Even if there is a mysterious principle, if you do not study and practice, you will not be able to know the profound beauty. In this life, the human body is the most fragile thing to lose,1 and the Buddha Dharma is the most difficult thing to hear and know.2 If the Tathagata had not come to this world to save sentient beings and widely spread the Buddha Dharma, surely both heaven and human worlds would still forever be immersed in the long night of ignorance and darkness.

NOTE 1

The Buddha taught: “Life is lost in just a breath.” People often don't pay attention, until death is near that they feel regret. Even if you breathe out at the same time as you breathe in, how can you be negligent and not try to practice when you can still practice?

NOTE 2

In the Sutras, the example of a blind turtle is often used to refer to the difficulty of people encountering the Buddhadharma. For example, in the sea there is a blind turtle, which only floats to the surface once every 100 years, and there is a piece of tree floating back and forth in that sea, which only passes by the blind turtle once every 100 years. The opportunity for each of us to be human and to hear about and believe in Buddhism is as difficult as a turtle finding a tree trunk to crawl into.

Not only crude people with narrow knowledge, but even Confucian scholars who have heard a lot, their knowledge is still limited, not comparable to Buddhism. Like looking up at the sky, people often think there is only one world with the sun,

the moon, without knowing that there are countless other worlds. Or we think that the first human was born in the Manu period, but we really don't know that in countless lifetimes from before until now, each of us has gone through countless lives. Or think that the Heavenly Emperors and Heavenly Immortals are the most noble beings, no one can compare, but really don't know that they are just ordinary people who have not escaped the cycle of reincarnation in the six realms.1 Or think that after death, the body decays and the soul dissipates, but really don't know that each of us already has a point of spiritual light, no matter how many lives we go through, we have never lost our clarity, how can it be destroyed?

NOTE 1

The six paths, or six paths, or six paths, refer to the six realms in which all sentient beings, due to karma, must circulate. The six realms include: the heavenly realm, the human realm, the asura realm, the hell realm, the hungry ghost realm, and the animal realm.

People think that once their parents or relatives have passed away, they can no longer do anything, but they don't know that once they learn this wonderful Buddha Dharma, even if they go through thousands of lives, they will know how to practice, often sowing good causes and reaping good results.

Or when you see good people facing difficulties, bad people getting their wishes, you immediately think that heaven is not worth believing in, but really do not know that everything is inspired by karma from previous lives, not even the slightest deviation.

How great, the classic Dharma of the Tathagata! It is truly a boat of compassion that carries many people through the ocean of suffering, a precious torch on a dark and gloomy road, a mother's milk at birth, rice in a year of poor harvest and famine. Therefore, when the Venerable Ananda compiled the Sutras, King Brahma and De Thich both held parasols to protect themselves, and the four Great Heavenly Kings personally knelt and held up the four-legged treasure throne. The world's books are truly incomparable, even in comparison. Therefore, printing and circulating scriptures is truly something that cannot be helped.

Before attaining enlightenment, the World-Honored One, for countless lifetimes, was willing to sacrifice his life and body for the sake of Buddha Dharma. Sometimes, he only prayed for a sutra or a verse and left his throne, or left his wife and children, there was nothing he couldn't do. Therefore, the Buddha's method is like a precious nectar, not always available in life. People in the world do not understand such preciousness and often underestimate the Buddhist scriptures, not knowing that even after a few thousand years, even if they want to pray for a single sentence or word in the scriptures, they will not be able to.

Dragon Praying for a French Boy

Once upon a time, there was a mandarin who guarded the royal garden. One day, he picked a rare fruit on the shore of the lake and immediately offered it to the king. The king liked it very much, so he ordered him to offer that fruit every day, otherwise he would be sentenced to death.

This official was frightened and unjustly cried out to heaven. At that time, in the lake there was a dragon king who appeared in human form, holding a golden tray of fruits, comforting the mandarin: "Don't be afraid anymore, bring this tray of fruits to the king, only asking for one thing. In the past, after Buddha Kasyapa entered Nirvana,1 this king and I together received the Eight Precepts.

NOTE 1

Buddha Kasyapa was born before Śākyamuni Buddha, at a time when the average human lifespan was 20,000 years. Author's Note)

The king kept the precepts and did not eat after noon, so in this life I was persuaded by others to eat after noon. That's why I fell into the dragon race If the king quickly brings that Dharma here, I will wholeheartedly help this country. Otherwise, I will drown the whole country."

But at that time there was no Buddha Dharma, so where could we find the Dharma of the Eight Precepts? The king was extremely worried and sad. At that time, the father of a great mandarin told him: "The pillar in my house often emits a bright halo, so try to split that pillar and see."

The minister listened to his father's words. When he split them, he immediately found two books of sutras: one book The Twelve Causes and Conditions and one book The Eight Precepts of Dharma. He immediately brought them to the king. The king was extremely happy and gave the book Eight Precepts to the Dragon King.

The Dragon King then together with his 500 children practiced the Eight Precepts Dharma. After death, all were reborn in the Dao Loi heaven.

Dharma of the Eight Precepts

First, do not kill: Any living thing must not be killed;

Second, do not steal: Anything that is not your own, if not given to you by someone else, you must not keep;

Third, abstain from lust: Five precepts of lay practitioners

The family only prohibits sexual immorality, but on the day of receiving the Eight Precepts, sexual immorality is completely stopped;

Fourth, do not lie: Words and thoughts must be the same, absolutely no deception;

Fifth, do not drink alcohol: Alcohol disrupts the mind, drinking causes all sins;

Friday, do not use incense, flowers for makeup, do not perfume your body: Because of eliminating greed and attachments, do not embellish and beautify your body;

Saturday, no music, singing, or dancing; Do not listen to or watch other people sing, sing, or dance: Play or sing yourself, or watch or listen to others play or sing, all will disrupt the mind of practice. Saying "dan ca" refers to the general use of all types of musical instruments such as lute, flute, flute, book...

Comment

In Duong Chau, there was a man named Nghiem Cung, in the first year of the Thai Kien year of the Tran dynasty1 copied the Lotus Sutra to pass down. At that time, a temple deity at Cung Dinh Lake gave a dream to a merchant, telling him to take all the property in the temple and bring it to Mr. Nghiem, so he could use it to copy sutras. Another day, Mr. Nghiem went to the market to buy paper but was short 3,000 VND. Suddenly he saw someone in the market bringing 3,000 VND, saying he was helping him buy paper. After speaking, he immediately disappeared.

NOTE 1

At the end of the Sui Dynasty, bandits came to Giang Do, telling each other not to trespass into Mr. Nghiem's village to copy the Lotus Sutra. Thanks to that, most of the villagers survived.

Gao Thien Huu, who Dinh Thuong district,

Anhui province, previously went with two classmates to Giang Ninh to take the exam. Everyone heard that Zen Master Thu Nguyen at Mount Ke Minh was a virtuous person, so they immediately invited each other to come and worship him.

The Zen master told the three people: "These two will both pass the exam, only Mr. Cao cannot pass because he was ignorant and used the Lang Nghiem Sutra as a pillow for his head."

Hearing that, Cao Thien Huu was very surprised, but calmly thought about it for a long time, then remembered that in the casket there was a set of Lang Nghiem Sutras, which he never took out when resting, but used that casket to rest his head.

When the exam results came out, it was exactly as the Zen master said.

Discussion

Some people wonder that all books and scriptures should be respected, why should only Buddhist scriptures be revered? Those people do not know that, although the words and meanings are the same, the Tathagata's teachings benefit all sentient beings, all eight classes of heaven and dragon, and no one does not believe and follow them, so ordinary books and bibliographies cannot compare. Just like the king's decree, it cannot be considered the same as other documents.

Considering the fact that Cao Thien Huu despised Buddhist scriptures and had to suffer the consequences of not passing the exam, then the person who was determined to print and circulate the Sutras would gain merit and benefits, one can certainly know what kind of merit and benefits it would bring.

CONSTRUCTION AND REPAIR OF TEMPLE
TEMP, MONASTERY

Extensive preaching

Buddha, Dharma and Sangha are the Three Jewels, the land Good fields for sentient beings to sow merit. But if you want to make solemn offerings to the Three Jewels, it can only be done in temples and monasteries. If there were no temples or monasteries, there would be no Buddha statues or Dharma scriptures. Monks and nuns in particular, and the four groups of Buddhists1 in general, even if they want to sow crops in the fields of blessings, worship and offer incense, receive, uphold, read and recite the Sutras, they still have no place to do so. Based on that, we know that the merit of those who build and repair pagodas and monasteries is extremely great.

NOTE 1

The four Buddhist communities include two monastic communities, the monks and nuns, and two lay communities, the upasakas (male lay followers) and upasakas (female lay followers).

The Sutra of the Dharma Foundation of Mindfulness2 teaches: "If any sentient being sees a damaged pagoda or tower and tries to repair it, and advises others to do the same, then after death they will be reborn in the heavenly world, with a bright and beautiful body, in the precious coral forest with the goddesses to enjoy the five sensual pleasures. When the heavenly karma has ended, they will be born as a human, their body will also be bright and beautiful. beautiful.”3

In the city of Xa-ve, there was a great rich man named Tu-atta-da,2 wanted to find a suitable place to build a monastery to worship Buddha. In the end, I only found the garden of Prince Ky-da, eighty plots wide, with lush green trees, truly the most suitable scenic spot.

Tu-datta immediately went to the prince and asked to buy it. The prince said: "If I spread the gold all over the garden, I will sell it to you." Tu-datta happily said: "If so, this garden will be mine." He immediately sent someone to carry the gold to spread it, and soon it was all over the garden. Seeing this, the Crown Prince immediately said: "I was just joking." Tu Dat replied: "You are a noble prince, you should not joke." Immediately determined to buy as much as he could, the crown prince finally agreed to sell.

The crown prince at that time did not accept the gold, but used that gold to build twelve hundred rooms in the monastery. Right while preparing the foundation for construction, Venerable Sariputta suddenly smiled. Tu-

Datta asked the reason, the Venerable replied: "Even though you have just started building a monastery here to make offerings to Buddha and monks, the blessings of the next life will be to enjoy the palace in heaven that has already been determined." After the Venerable finished speaking, he immediately used his supernatural powers to make Tu-datta suddenly have heavenly eyes and observe the palace in heaven. tieu_de: Drinking water helps quench people's thirst
noi_dung:
GIVING DRINK WATER TO RESET

THISTHY FOR PEOPLE

Preaching widely

Everyone knows that being too hungry can lead to death, but did not know that thirst can also cause illness. For strong young people, they can endure it, but for weak old people, it is difficult to survive. For people who are healthy, they can normally endure it, but for people with many illnesses, it will be very difficult to endure. For people who are close by, it can be tolerable, but for people traveling far away, it is very difficult to overcome the thirst. When the weather is mild and cool, it is bearable, but when it is cold or hot, it is not easy to endure.

The ancients taught: "Don't criticize a small good deed

without doing it."1 Providing water to quench someone's thirst is also one of the small good deeds that should be done.

NOTE 1

According to Tam Quoc Chi, this is Liu Bei's last words before his death, instructing his son Liu Thien, including 2 sentences: 勿以善小而不為， 勿以惡小而為之 - What is good is not a child, what is evil is not a child. (Do not criticize small good deeds without doing them, do not despise small evil deeds and commit them.)

Cite the story

THE BLESSING OF HELPING DRINKING WATER FOR PEOPLE2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the Sutra of Hundred Fates (百緣經). (Author's note) The full name of this sutra is Compilation of Hundred Sutras (撰集百緣經), included in the new Dai Chanh tu tu Dai Tripitaka, in volume 4, sutra number 200, a total of 10 volumes, translated by Mr. Chi Khiem in the Wu dynasty. This story is briefly recounted from the 85th cause and effect in the sutra, which is Da-xa-mat-da-condition (耶舍蜜多緣), starting from the 7th line, page 246, sheet b, volume 9. You can see this story in the Vietnamese translation with the name One Hundred Stories of Buddhist Cause and Effect, translated and annotated by Doan Trung Con - Nguyen Minh Tien Viet, Religion Publishing House, 2010, pages 299 - 302. The original An Si Complete Book had some details that were different. During the translation, we edited it based on the scriptures to make it more accurate.

During the Buddha's time, in the city of Savatthi, there was an extremely wealthy businessman. His wife gave birth to a handsome and beautiful son. Since birth, he never drank mother's milk. From between his teeth, he naturally secreted water with eight merits and used it to nourish himself.3

NOTE 3

Water has all eight merits (eight merits of water), that is, it has all eight properties: 1. Pure: clear and clear; 2. Cold: clear and cool; 3. Orange: sweet taste; 4. Light and soft: gentle and soft; 5. Nhuan Trach: imbues freshness; 6. Peaceful: peaceful and gentle; 7. Eliminate hunger and thirst and countless sufferings; 8. Nurture the body of the four great elements and grow good roots. In the Amitabha Sutra, this type of water is mentioned in the world of Ultimate Bliss: "舍利弗極樂國土有七寶池，八功德水充滿其 中 - Sāriputra! The Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss has many preservations, the eight merit waters are abundant in the middle." (Sariputta! In the Pure Land there is a pond built of seven treasures, filled with water of eight merits.)

That son's name was Da-xa-mat-da. Later, when he grew up, he followed Buddha and became a monk,1 practiced and attained Arhatship. A Bhikkhu asked the Buddha about Da-xa-mat-da's past life. The Buddha taught: "At the time of Buddha Kasyapa in the past, there was an old and weak wealthy man who had just become a monk. He was also seriously ill, so he could not diligently practice. The doctor advised him to use condensed milk mixed with medicine. At night, that medicine made his whole body hot, his mouth was dry, and he was extremely thirsty. He woke up to look for water. drank but found no water everywhere. Finally, he ran to the riverbank to find water, but unexpectedly found that the river had dried up. He had to endure extreme thirst.

NOTE 1

According to the Complete Book of An Si, this person was named Da-xa-mat-da after becoming a monk, but according to the scriptures, this was the name given to him by his parents since childhood. This name is transliterated from Sanskrit as Yacomitra, meaning "very honored". The reason for this name is because when he was born, it rained heavily. Everyone thought it was because of the baby's blessings, so his parents immediately named him that way. We have edited this detail according to the scriptures.

“The next day he told his teacher about not being able to find drinking water. His teacher said: 'The suffering you describe is very similar to the suffering in the realm of hungry ghosts. Now take the water from my vase and try it.' The Bhikkhu listened to the teacher and went to get the water from the vase. When he arrived, he looked again and saw water in the vase.

naturally dried up. That monk was extremely worried and frightened, knowing that after death he would definitely fall into the realm of hungry ghosts. He immediately went to pay homage to Buddha Kassapa, sincerely repenting all his previous sins. Buddha Kasyapa taught: 'From now on, you should focus on providing clean water for the monks to use, so you can escape the evil karma of being born into the realm of hungry ghosts.'

" That monk heard the Buddha's teachings with great joy, from then on, he constantly focused on providing clean water for the monks to use, until his lifespan was 20,000 years. that's it.1

NOTE 1

The average lifespan of people at the time of Buddha Kassapa in the past was 20,000 years (Author's note)

“Due to that cause and effect, from then on this Bhikkhu was born anywhere, in the middle of nowhere. Teeth also often secrete water that has all eight merits. To this day, I have met Buddha, left home to practice and attained enlightenment.”

Comment

The sentient beings in the realm of hungry ghosts, through many lifetimes, have not even heard the name of water, they just have no water to drink. Hungry ghost beings, such as those born next to a river, still do not hear the name of water. If Bhikkhu Da-xa-mat-da had not met Tathagata Kasyapa before, how could he have turned misfortune into blessing like that?

USE WATER TO SELL POOR LIFE1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Sutra of Wise and Foolish Cause and Effect (賢愚因緣經). (Author's note) The name of this sutra in the Dai Chanh new revision of the Great Tripitaka is Hien Ngu Kinh (賢愚經), belonging to volume 4, sutra number 202, a total of 13 volumes, translated by Hui Giac's group from Sanskrit to Chinese during the Yuan Wei dynasty. This story is abridged from the sutra called Ca-chien-dien Giao old mother mai bo - 迦旃延教老母賣貧品, starting from line 29, page 383, sheet c, in volume 5.

In the country of A-ban-de, there was a wealthy man who had countless wealth, but was extremely stingy, so that the maid in the house had to live in extreme poverty, not enough clothes to cover her body, not enough food to fill her stomach, and was often beaten and tortured even though she was old and weak. That person wants to die to escape suffering but cannot die.

One ​​day, that old maid brought a jar to the river bank to get water, felt sorry for herself and cried bitterly. A Buddhist disciple, Mr. Ca-chan-dien, saw this and felt sorry for him and immediately asked: "If the old lady hates her life of poverty, why doesn't she sell it?"

The old slave replied: "Who would buy something poor?"

Mr. Ka-chan-dien said: "Yes, the old woman's poverty can indeed be sold."

The old slave immediately asked: "How can I sell it?"

The old servant asked: "This vase is the owner's property, not mine, how can I offer it?"

Mr. Ca-chien-dien replied: "Even though the vase is not yours, do you not have the right to use the water in the vase?"

The old woman understood and immediately brought a vase to get water to offer. Ca-chien-dien personally received that offering, then taught her the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, and then taught her to recite Buddha's name.

That night, the old lady died in her master's house. In the morning, the owner saw this and became angry, took the body and threw it into the Cold Forest.1 The old woman's consciousness was then born in the Dao-loi heaven, as a celestial being there. Seeing the old body from afar, she and her celestial relatives immediately appeared to sprinkle heavenly flowers on that body.

NOTE 1

Originally used Academician (cold forest), referring to a forest located outside of Vuong Xa citadel, the original Sanskrit name is Śītavana, the phonetic translation is Thi-da-ba-na, so it is also called Thi-da forest. This forest has long been used by people in Rajagaha city as a place to throw away corpses that have not been buried, to be fed to animals.

Comment

If you know that practicing almsgiving can "sell poverty", of course you will know that paying homage to the Buddhas can "sell poverty", practicing releasing animals can "sell poverty". away from premature death", diligent learning can "sell ignorance". People with wisdom can understand a hundred thousand things just by hearing one thing. With all the unsatisfactory adversities in this world, is there anything that cannot be "sold" like that?

tieu_de: Or spend money to buy live animals to release
noi_dung:
OR GIVE UP MONEY TO BUY LIVING ANIMALS
RELEASE LIFE

Preaching

The law punishes criminals, there is no punishment worse than death; Parents who love their children do nothing more than give and nurture life to the fullest. Therefore, we can know that the most evil thing is to kill, and the most kind thing is to save lives and release lives. Look at when the animals are chased, they also run away in fear, let out pitiful screams, and try their best to climb the fence and climb the wall in the hope of escaping. If we compare it to us humans, when the king orders us to arrest and kill, our parents are terrified and don't know what to do, and our wives and children are pushed into death with no way out. How is that fear any different?

Look again when an animal is killed, like when cutting the blood of a chicken, the whole flock of chickens screams in terror, slaughtering a pig, the whole herd of pigs sadly stops eating. If we compare it to us humans, when we encounter chaos and bandits, we see our parents being murdered, our wives and children being kidnapped and taken away, that tragic situation is no different.

And consider when an animal is cut up for slaughter, its intestines and liver are exposed while the mouth is still whispering breath, or the throat has been cut off but the eyes are still wide open before

aim. If compared to us humans, when we are in pain and suffering, our whole body is motionless, we only know how to look, and we are helpless, what difference does it make?

If at that moment we callously kill, how can the resentment of the killed animal be said to end? If at that time someone had spent money to save their lives and released them, what would be the end of the gratitude?

The release of animals should not be done on a regular basis, for fear that someone will know the date we bought the released animals and will try their best to catch them and sell them. You should also not choose a fixed location to release animals, lest someone find out and wait after you release the living creatures and then try to capture them again. Releasing animals is not limited to any animal, no matter how big or small they are, they should be saved.

Of the animal release associations in the Kunlun area where I live, only Thanh Luong hermitage is the best, because since its inception, a good friend first spent a large amount of money, depositing it to earn interest, 1 each month uses that interest to release animals. Each time a life release is organized, about 4 or 5 days before, a report is sent to each member to inform them of the amount of money used. When the deadline is due, the members share and donate to cover the full amount spent, completely without relying on the profitable deposit amount. Thanks to that, it can work for a long time. Go to

NOTE 1

Originally used the word dien pho (典鋪), synonymous with dong pho (當鋪), meaning pawn shop. Here it can be understood as depositing money there to earn monthly interest.

on the day of the release festival, each person respectfully recites 5 volumes of the Avatamsaka Sutra,1 the cost of incense and water camellia is shared by three people. It is thanks to all members working together that the association's activities are successful and can be a model for other places to follow.

NOTE 1

The full name is the Dai Phuong Quang Phat Hoa Nghiem Sutra (大方廣佛華嚴 經), currently included in the new Dai Chanh revised Tripitaka with 3 translations, the translation by Buddha-da-bat-da-la is in volume 9, sutra number 278, a total of 60 book, translated in the Eastern Jin Dynasty; The version translated by Thana-nan-da in the Tang Dynasty belongs to volume 10, sutra number 279, a total of 80 volumes, and the version translated by Bat Nha during the Tang dynasty belongs to volume 10, sutra number 293, a total of 40 volumes. Each person recites 5 books, which means dividing them among themselves to continue reciting the entire sutra.

Citing the story

Sparing the pig2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book Phap Uyen Chau Lam (法苑珠林). (Author's note) However, we have not found this story in Phap Uyen Chau Lam as cited in this note, but only found it appearing in two other works: Tap Shen Chau Three Jewels Sympathy Luc (集神州三寶感通錄), included in Dai Chanh's newly revised Tripitaka in volume 52, sutra number 2106, a total of three volumes, compiled by Mr. Dao Tuyen in the Tang Dynasty, this story begins. starting from the 23rd line, page 433, page a, in volume 3, and in the Six Dao Taps (六道集), included in the Van Tan Toan Tuc Kinh, in volume 88, sutra number 1645, a total of five volumes, compiled by Mr. Hong Tan in the Qing Dynasty, this story starts from line 23, page 150, page c, in volume 4. Both of these books talk in more detail. About the person's name: this man's real name is Do Nguyen, his personal name is Vinh Binh.

During the Eastern Jin Dynasty, there was a man named Do Vinh Binh, a native of Phu Chau, Tu Dong district, Sichuan province. Mr. Binh's family is very rich, they have a son named Thien Bao, just 10 years old, who loves him very much. In the third year of the Thai Nguyen era,3 Thien Bao became seriously ill and died. Not long after

NOTE 3

That is the year 378.

there, in the house there was a sow that gave birth to five cubs. Vinh Binh chose the fattest one and planned to slaughter it as an offering to the mandarins. Suddenly a Bhikkhu came and said to Vinh Binh: "That pig was your son, why did you forget it just over a hundred days ago?" As soon as the monk finished speaking, he suddenly disappeared, leaving behind only a strange, fragrant scent that has not dissipated all day.

Do Vinh Binh immediately released the pig, did not kill it, but lovingly raised it in the house.

Commentary

The Buddha taught: "All sentient beings, through many reincarnations, are most of each other's parents and relatives." Readers of Confucian books do not know the principle of reincarnation in the three lives of past, present and future. Therefore, one should not bear the idea of ​​considering all sentient beings as one's many-life parents. But then because I can't bear to think like that, I kill living beings to make my own food. Is that called not being able to bear it? To generalize, it's because you don't think carefully.

SELLING PIGS TO SELL CHILDREN1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from Ming Bao Ky (冥報記). (Author's note)

During the Sui Dynasty, around the 8th year of Dai Nghiep era,2 in Nghi Chau district, Guangxi province, someone named Hoang Phu Thien stole 60 copper coins

NOTE 2

That is in the year 612.

Mom's money. The mother lost money and couldn't find it. The investigation and questioning caused everyone in the family to be beaten.

The next year, Phu Thien died and was reborn as a pig in the house. When the pig grew up, the family immediately sold it to the village chief in a far away village for six hundred dong. That night, Phu Thien's wife had just fallen asleep when she dreamed of a pig and said: "I am your husband before, because he stole sixty coins from his mother, causing the whole family to be whipped. Because of that crime, he had to be born as a pig, and now he is being sold. I hope you will redeem me quickly, otherwise I will be slaughtered."

The wife woke up startled, completely in disbelief. But when I fell asleep again, I had the same dream, and I heard the pig urging me even more urgently. When I woke up, I thought the situation was urgent, so I immediately put on my shirt and knocked on my mother-in-law's door. It turned out that Phu Thien's mother had also woken up a long time ago, because she had the same dream as her. It was past midnight, and the pig-buying village chief's house was thirty miles away. The mother was afraid that she could not redeem the pig, so she took out 1,200 denarii and sent her eldest son to go with Phu Thien's son to redeem it. Who would have thought that the village's sacrifice had already been arranged properly, so the village chief absolutely refused to allow the pig to be redeemed.

While it was still dark, Phu Thien's family immediately asked a group of powerful thugs to force the commune chief to redeem it. The village chief was reluctant to resist, so he let the pig go. On the way home, when

passed a large wasteland, the eldest brother immediately said to the pig: "If it's really my brother, go ahead." The pig immediately ran forward, following the correct path home.

After that, the neighbors who heard about it all laughed and gossiped. Phu Thien's children were very embarrassed, thought about it and discussed with each other: "If I leave my father like this, no one in the family will look at the girls. In the past, my father was very close to the Tu family, he could send it to them, we would periodically provide food."

The pig heard those words, tears flowed freely, immediately wagged his tail and went to the Tu family's house, forty miles away. In the 11th year of Dai Nghiep,1 the pig died in the Tu family.

NOTE 1

That is the year 615.

Comment

Once the shape has changed, all family members cannot recognize it. Therefore, it can be said that, in the world of reincarnation, family and relatives are ultimately only temporary, not real relationships.

SAVE THE GOAT TURNS OUT TO SAVE THE DAUGHTER2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book Phap Uyen Chau Lam (法苑珠林). (Author's note) The book Phap Uyen Chau Lam (法苑珠林) was included in the Dai Chanh new revision of the Tripitaka in volume 53, sutra number 2122, a total of 100 volumes, compiled by Dao The in the Tang Dynasty. This story starts from the 29th line, page 486, sheet c, volume 74. In addition, this story is also recorded in the book Mingbaoji (冥報記), included in the Dai Chanh new revision of the Tripitaka in volume 51, sutra number 2082, a total of three volumes, compiled by Duong Lam in the Tang Dynasty, starting from line 17, page 798, sheet a, volume 3.

In the Tang Dynasty, in Chang'an there was the following custom

Tet is when everyone takes turns organizing a banquet to entertain guests. There was a stationery store owner named Trieu Dai. It was his turn to host a party and invite guests home. On that day, as soon as the guests arrived, they saw a girl about 13-14 years old above the rice mortar, tied to a rope, wearing blue pants and a white shirt. The little girl cried and told the guests: "I am the daughter of the owner of this house. A year ago I stole a hundred denarii from my parents, intending to use it to buy makeup, but died before I could buy it. That money is still left in the kitchen, in a hole in the northwest corner. Because of that crime, I now have to become a goat."

As soon as the little girl finished speaking, the guests looked closely and only saw a blue goat with a white head. Everyone panicked and reported it to the homeowner, Trieu Dai. Trieu asked about the baby's appearance. It was indeed very similar to his daughter, who died two years ago. Immediately went to look in the kitchen, sure enough, there was money still lying where the girl said. Trieu Dai immediately brought the goat to the temple to release it, and made a vow from then on that the whole family would keep the precepts and become vegetarian.

Comment

The stolen money is still unused, and the miserable retribution has already come, but it is not an unjust crime. That is truly:

Hundreds of thousands of things are left behind,
Only karma is still carried.

Considering that, I believe in cause and effect even more deeply.

HITTING THE HORSE TURNS TO BEAT THE MOTHER1

NOTE 1

Excerpt from the book Ming Pao Shi Di (冥報拾遺). (Author's note)

During the Tang Dynasty, in Van Thuy district of Tinh Chau,2 there was a man named Ly Tin, who worked as a bodyguard in Long Chinh palace. One winter during the reign of Hien Khanh in the reign of Emperor Gaozong,3 Ly Tin as usual went to Soc Chau to take up a job. When he went, he rode a red horse signed4, leading a colt. At that time, the weather was very cold, the wind was cold, and the snow was falling heavily. After traveling more than ten miles, the horse could not take a step. Ly Tin used a whip to whip the horse. At the tenth whip, the horse suddenly spoke like a human, telling Ly Tin: "I was your mother before. Because when I was alive, I betrayed your father and stole more than one rice jelly for my little daughter, so now I have to suffer this retribution. That young horse is your younger sister, who received the stolen rice the other day, so now she also has to pay the retribution."

NOTE 2

This is now Shanxi province.

NOTE 3

The Xianqing era lasted from 656 to 661.

NOTE 4

The signed horse is a good horse breed, can travel thousands of miles a day, is very tame, easy to control.

Ly Tin couldn't hold back his tears when he heard it, so he took off the reins and saddle, carried it himself and said to the horse: "If it's really my mother, please go home." The horse immediately followed the path back home.

From then on, the Ly Tin brothers immediately built a separate house to raise that horse and take care of it together. There was a colleague of hers who used to often make offerings to monks and repentance ceremonies because of her. Since then, Ly Tin's entire family has diligently practiced and practiced.

The Minister of Justice, On Nhu An, and the Justice of Ky Chau, Truong Kim Dinh, were both at home mourning their parents. When they heard about this, they were surprised and frightened. They went to the place to question them, and sure enough, they found the horse was still there.

Discussion

Money and wealth can be used together. There is certainly no place better than in a family where husband, wife, and children are together. Yet, stealing from the family still has to be severely punished, with no deviation. Those who, as parents, love and hate their children unfairly, show favoritism to their children, take what belongs to one child and give it to another, should use that as a warning to themselves, isn't that scary?

long, came and said: "I am General Cao Han of the Song Dynasty.1 Previously, in the Tang Dynasty,2 I was a merchant. After that, Ung Chi immediately said to Tu Chieu: "From now on, I would like to concentrate on practicing." Those who follow Confucianism, because they are greedy for good food, often cite that Confucius is not a vegetarian, to justify their eating meat and drinking wine. So how can it be said that Confucius never advised against eating meat and drinking alcohol? Confucianism also advocates that before each ceremony, one must practice pure precepts, because fasting and keeping the precepts will help keep the body and mind pure, thus being able to communicate with the gods. From this it can be inferred that eating meat and drinking alcohol makes people drowsy. People today cannot act like Confucius. If they only want to follow Confucius in not being vegetarian, how can they enter the holy gate?

SELLING VEGETARIAN WORKS IMMEDIATELY LOSE YOUR LIFE2

dirty, dirty things, so the food is like

so it is indeed impure;

tieu_de: When taking steps, you must observe and do not step on insects
noi_dung:
MUST BE OBSERVED AT FIRST STEPS,
DON'T TRADE ON INSECTS
Insects

Explain widely

People in life also have things Those who know how to pity buffaloes, goats, dogs, horses... But if it comes to pitying insects, ants, termites... many people will laugh and call them stupid. That's because people don't know how to consider that, although the physical form is different in size, the nature of all living things is not big or small. If you think that killing large animals is a greater sin, but killing small animals is not a sin, then surely although humans are big, they are still smaller than buffalos, so instead of killing buffalos, wouldn't it be better to kill humans? If we look at it that way,

the most noble person in the world must be the giant fish1, not humans, because they are the biggest.

This teaching of Emperor Quan is to help everyone get rid of the above discriminatory view of big and small towards living things, so that every time they take a step, they must be cautious and not dare to accidentally commit killing.

People in this world can't help but commit sins. Just taking the matter of walking alone, over the course of a lifetime, countless thousands of lives have been harmed... I once saw in the book The Law of novices, there are verses and notes talking about walking without harming insects and ants. It's very simple but has an extremely profound meaning. Every early morning, before lying down in bed, you should recite a few verses of Buddha's name, then single-mindedly read the verse:

從朝寅旦直至暮，
一切眾生自回護，

Tung trieu gradually dan chi to the grave,
All sentient beings will recover themselves.
Thuoc u tuc will encounter trauma,2

Prayer immediately be born in the Pure Land.

Children from about 6 or 7 years old should be taught to act and think this way. Over time, it becomes a habit and routine, so the concept of kindness will soon be cultivated from childhood. Mencius said: “The early morning rooster immediately rose up, concentrated on nurturing and cultivating the good mind to increasingly

grow larger.” By doing as above, wouldn't it be even more helpful for Mencius' teachings?

Citing the story

One ​​person said: "We should drink this water, because that will save our bodies, and then we can go see the Buddha and listen to the Dharma."

The other immediately said: "If you don't keep the precepts established by the Buddha, then what's the use of going to see the Buddha?" Immediately starved and died. This person's consciousness was immediately born in the Dao Loi heaven. This person, knowing the causes and conditions before being born in heaven, immediately brought incense and flowers to the Ky Vien monastery to make offerings to the Buddha.

The other monk drank water containing insects so he did not die of thirst. The next day, he reached Ky Vien, cried and reported his suffering to the Buddha, mentioning his companion who had died of thirst.

Buddha taught: “I already know.” He immediately raised his hand to point at the god who had just come to make offerings and said: "This is the friend who was with you the other day and has come here. You came here to only see my external appearance, but did not keep the precepts that I established, so even though you said you came to meet me, I actually did not meet you. This sentence, according to the scriptures, supplements the full meaning of the Buddha's teachings. Because the An Si Complete Book summarizes it, there is a lack of meaning.

Comment

Buddha taught the monks that empty jars, jars... should be turned upside down or covered, not left face up. Why? Because when left upside down without covering it, of course it will contain rainwater, thereby giving birth to insects. When someone uses it, pouring the water out means killing those insects.

During the summer and autumn, rainwater accumulates in puddles on the ground, and after a day or two, insects will inevitably appear in the water. Most of those insects die when the water runs out. Therefore, you should clear the drains so that there is no

anywhere around the house

water stagnates into a puddle. Do not use standing water in sewers to water plants or flowers, because drying water will also kill many insects in it. Do not throw fish bones, meat, or leftover food that has a fishy smell... indiscriminately on the ground, because doing so will attract ants, which will surely be trampled to death. LIVING THE BODY TO SAVE ALL SPECIES2

NOTE 2

Buddha taught: "At that time, I was a king deer with an extremely large body and strength. Discussion

After retelling this story, the Buddha taught: "All the animals that I saved from crossing the river in the past are now my disciples. The last rabbit to cross the river is now Mr. Tu-bat-da."1

tieu_de: At night, pedestrians have lights to illuminate the road

DARK NIGHTS HELP PEOPLE TO TRAVEL THE ROAD IS LIGHTED WITH LIGHT

Preaching widely

During the dark night it was difficult to walk, suddenly there was a light. light, it's like a blind person suddenly regaining his sight, and just like when the sky is dark but he can retain a little bit of the sunset to illuminate the entire earth. For people who are in a situation where they have to walk in the dark, what greater blessing is there?

The person walking in the night has a light and can clearly see everything ahead to easily move forward. Therefore, those who use torches to bring light to help others will certainly be blessed with clear eyes.

Furthermore, when walking at night with a bright light, there will no longer be anxiety or fear in your heart. Therefore, those who use torches to bring light to help others will certainly receive blessings full of joy and joy.

Furthermore, when walking at night with a bright light, you won't have to step on muddy places. Therefore, those who use torches to bring light to help others will certainly receive blessings and always be clean and pure.

Furthermore, when walking at night with a bright light, you will certainly hear the sound of a dog barking without panic or fear. Therefore, those who use torches to bring light to help others will certainly receive blessings and be always peaceful and fearless.

Moreover, when walking at night with a bright light, others will certainly not suspect that they are evil people. Therefore, those who use torches to bring light to help others will certainly receive blessings and often act righteously.

Furthermore, when walking at night with a bright light, you will definitely not stumble and cause injury. Therefore, those who

use torches to bring light to help others will certainly receive the blessing of being free from illness and suffering, and having a strong and healthy body.

Furthermore, when walking at night with a bright light, there will be no danger of falling into ditches, streams, pits, wells... Therefore, those who use torches to bring light to help others will certainly be blessed with a long life.

At night, helping people on the road have a light to illuminate, they will certainly receive many benefits as above, it cannot be said that it is simply illuminating the way for people walking. Is that okay?

People are ignorant, they are born without knowing where they come from, and when they die they really don't know where they will go. In a moment he entered a fetus, and in a moment he exited a fetus. Everything is circulating in a dark place. Who has the bright light to illuminate the path?

Buddha taught that:

欲知前世因，
今生受者是；
欲知後世果，
今生作者是。

Knowing the people of the past,
The golden life lives on verse;
Education knows the consequences of life,
The author's life is born.

Temporarily translated:

Want to know the causes of previous lives,
Look at the results today.
If you want to know the results in the next life,
Look at the causes of this life.

If you follow this teaching correctly and reflect, then naturally the previous life and the next life will all be as bright as if there was a shining light. People who practice according to the Ten Good Virtues and follow this reflection will clearly see that they will definitely be born in heaven. Those who observe the Five Precepts, following this reflection, will clearly see that they will definitely be born in the human world. People who have taken refuge in the Three Jewels, following this reflection will clearly see that they will no longer fall into the Three Evil Paths. Contemplating like that means having the lamp of wisdom.

tieu_de: The wide river helps boats carry people back and forth
noi_dung:
WIDE RIVER HELPS BOATS
BRING PEOPLE BACK AND BACK Extensive preaching

While on the way, we encountered a river blocking the way and had to stop, confused and not knowing how to plan, still lamenting why we were only one line away. A river that is more difficult to cross than a thousand miles of travel, but suddenly a boat takes you across the river. That's where the road to life opens up at a dead end. Those who help others from a remote place to get life, surely they themselves will also get a way to life from a remote place.

In a wide river that can help people cross, of course there is great merit. In the sea of ​​suffering of life and death, if you can help someone cross the river, the merit is much greater.

Bringing someone across the river, that favor is only temporary. Bringing people across the sea of ​​suffering of life and death, that grace will indeed last for generations and generations.

All of us mortals are on this side of the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death, and only thanks to the six great deeds can we cross over to the other shore of enlightenment. That other shore is the shore of liberation of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who have escaped beyond the Three Realms. The six great virtues are practicing according to the six paramitas. That is, the virtue of father paramita of generosity helps us overcome the sea of ​​greed and stinginess; The virtue of paramita morality helps us overcome the ocean of negative karma; The perfection of patience helps us overcome the ocean of anger; The paramita of diligence helps us overcome the sea of ​​laziness and indulgence; The virtue of meditation paramita of concentration helps us overcome the sea of ​​mental confusion; The virtue of paramita of wisdom helps us overcome the sea of ​​ignorance and delusion.

Citing the story

HARD EFFORT TO SAVE THE DROWNING PERSON1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Y Hanh Luc (懿行錄). (Author's note)

and their descendants will be rich and glorious, so they should be reburied in this land..." Saying that, he pointed to a place of land. The family followed the instructions of the Taoist and reburied him. That place later became known to geographers as Bach To Mound.

That is the year 1696.

you can see that by doing your best to benefit others, you will never be at a disadvantage for yourself; I put all my effort into greed for material things, but in the end, I didn't get any. tieu_de: No nets to catch terrestrial birds and animals
noi_dung:
NO NETS TO CATCH SPECIES
LAND BIRDS1

NOTE 1

The original text is “勿登山而網禽獸” (Do not go up the mountain with a net to catch birds and animals). But in the past, people only went to the mountains and forests to spread nets, but today this practice happens anywhere, even right in the middle of the city, where many birds gather and nets are caught. Therefore, we have translated the meaning accordingly.

Explanation

Even though they are the same species with winged feathers, birds and animals are very different from livestock, chickens and ducks. Then he brought it to Ty-xa-ly's house and gave one tree to each of his 32 children.

Later, he secretly reported to the king that the 32 children of Mr. Ty-xa-ly, relying on the power of the world that no one could defeat them, secretly intended to rebel, and now hid sharp knives inside horsewhips, waiting for the opportunity to strike. The king let investigators see that there was indeed a sharp knife hidden in the horse's whip, so he believed his words and immediately ordered the arrest of the 32 brothers of the Pi-xa-ly family and beheaded them all. tieu_de: Do not throw away paper with writing on it
noi_dung:
DO NOT THROW AWAY PAPER WITH WRITING

Preaching

Humans can become the most noble of all creatures because their mouths can speak. words and hands can write. Hands that can write literature are considered hands that can speak words. But the words that come out of the mouth can only be heard by those close to them, while written literature can be transmitted thousands of miles away. Words spoken from the mouth can only be heard temporarily, but literature can be passed down forever to posterity. Words from the mouth must be heard with the ears, while literature can be read with the eyes. When words come out of the mouth, the listener feels tired for a moment, but the literature left behind will not tire the reader for thousands of generations.

Therefore, how great a contribution real writing has to humans! In this world, if there were no writing, mandarins would have nothing to rely on to rule the people, and the orders given would have no evidence. So not only can we not have peace at home, but we also can't keep our affairs in order. People are so indebted to writing, how can they contemptuously throw away paper with writing on it?

Paper with writing on it of course cannot be thrown away, even more so the meaning of the writing cannot be thrown away. Like someone who disobeys their parents, that is throwing away the meaning of the word "filial piety" for a lifetime; If you don't treat your brothers and sisters well, that means throwing away the meaning of the word "nice" for the rest of your life. Just like that, considering each point in turn, there must be quite a few meanings of writing that we have thrown away!

There are people who use paper with writing on it to wrap goods, tape windows, and then throw it away, thinking that the things they throw away are just paper with writing on it. There are also people who doubt that the story of Cang Jie creating writing, opening up the source of writing for all generations, it is reasonable for the sky to rain down rice, but why are there stories of ghosts and gods crying at night?1 That is because we really do not know that, if the world's writing has a legitimate use, there must also be an evil use. Because of the righteous use, it rains rice and grain, but because of the evil use, ghosts and gods cry at night.

NOTE 1

The book Hoai Nam Tu - The Sutra of Teachings records that: "In the past, Shangjie created writing, the sky rained down rice, and ghosts and gods cried at night."

Citing the story

THE BURGING SUTRA WAS AUTOMATICALLY1

NOTE 1

Collected from the book Gong pass the way (功過格). (Author's note)

In Shaanxi province, to the west of Wugong district, there is a temple, in the temple there was once a damaged collection of Buddhist scriptures. When he was a teenager, Khang Doi Son2 once went with five school friends to the temple to read books. At that time, it was cold winter weather, four of them took torn prayer books and burned them for warmth, one person burned them to boil water to wash their face. Khang Doi Son in his heart criticized those people but did not dare to say it out loud.

NOTE 2

Khang Doi Son, whose name is Hai, passed the exam during the reign of Thanh Hoa (1465-1487) during the reign of Minh Tuyen Tong. He is a literary man, his virtues are perfect.

That night, Doi Son dreamed that there were three mandarins setting up a solemn court for trial. They all expressed anger and indignation at those who burned scriptures to warm themselves, saying: "Your entire family will die, with no descendants." Then he turned to the person who burned the sutras and boiled the water and said, "In the future you will never be glorified." They reprimanded Khuong Doi Son, saying: "Why did you see that and not say anything?" Doi Son replied: "I'm younger than them. Even though I know I shouldn't do that, I don't dare say it." The official said: "A word of advice or explanation can also exonerate you. But for now, I will forgive you."

Khuong Doi Son woke up and immediately copied this story into the back of a book to remember. Not

a few years later, all four people who used to use the fire to keep warm were infected with an epidemic that killed the whole family. As for the person who burns scriptures to boil water, after many exams he faces difficulties, in the end he only spends his whole life struggling with the profession of teaching children.

Discussion

Worldly books can be burned when they are damaged and can no longer be read, but Buddhist scriptures cannot be burned in any case. Because Buddhist scriptures bring blessings and wisdom to people, far beyond all worldly books. Even though they are the same word, the meanings within them can be heavy, light, light, and weighty, with world-wide differences, not the same at all. As the exemplary astronomical chapters of classics, mo, vows, and statements in the Sutras, of course they cannot be classified in the same category as literary novels.

Nowadays, when comparing literate people with illiterate people, literate people are considered better; If we take a person who is semi-literate and compare it with a person who is well-educated and has a broad understanding of the past, the person who is well-educated and has a broad understanding must be considered superior. Worldly books can only talk about worldly affairs, they cannot clearly understand what is beyond this heaven. If a broad person reads many Buddhist scriptures, he will surely be able to understand the miraculous stories in dragon palaces, under the sea, far away, he can understand the stories of past and future lives, to the immensity of countless lands in the ten directions, all such things can be understood through general outlines, and the ambition is also nurtured far beyond ordinary people.

For illiterate people, if you tell them about the rule of the country by the kings of Tang, Ngu, Three Greats, or names like Nghieu, Shun, Zhou, Kong... they will certainly be extremely surprised when they hear it. Likewise, for people who have only read worldly books, if they were allowed to listen to the words in the Buddhist Tripitaka, what the Buddha taught for forty-nine years, they would also be surprised and find it difficult to consider. Such tendencies are natural.

Accordingly, if the teachings on causes and conditions to abandon evil and cultivate good deeds are only transmitted outside the canon, which are scriptures spoken by the Buddha, if burned and thrown away, how can one not commit a sin? What's more, if you look down on it enough to use it for heating or to boil water, you will surely fall into hell forever, suffering forever and ever, with no time to escape. In this life alone, losing the whole family and falling into poverty is truly not enough to pay for all the cruel sins.

Question: If the scriptures are intact, of course you cannot burn them, but what if the scriptures are damaged?

Answer: If it is so damaged that it can no longer be read, you can burn it, then use a clean bag to contain the ashes and scatter them into the rivers and seas. As the swastika is the heart seal of the Tathagata, it cannot be underestimated.

PUMPING ASH IN THE LAND SHOULD REDUCE THE LIFE1

NOTE 1

Also collected from the book Cong Qua Ca (功過格). (Author's note)

In Tra Khe town, Tan Hoa district, Hunan province, there is a person named Chu Ninh Uoc, whose nickname is Sy Phong, who is very

like calligraphy. During the reign of Khang Hy in the Qing Dynasty, in the second month of the year At Suu,1 he suddenly fell ill and died, and his close friends all came to mourn.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1685.

Suddenly he came back to life and told everyone: "My lifespan was originally 42 years, but because I diligently practiced writing every day, wrote it and then arbitrarily burned it, carried the ashes and dumped them indiscriminately, without any respect or regret. The underworld recorded that mistake of mine, reducing my lifespan by 5 years, so now at the age of 37 my life is over. You should know, when burning paper with writing, you must be careful not to dump ashes indiscriminately. beach.”

After speaking, he closed his eyes and died.

Buddha taught King Up-dien:2 “In this world, there are people who are passionate about female beauty, often fantasizing about women's beauty, and therefore are controlled by their desires, like servants who are always afraid of their masters. Because of their desire for female beauty, they cannot see the impurity from the nine holes in the human body, 3 always focus on lust, love dirty phlegm, enjoy the smell of blood and pus, consider them as precious as pearls, sweet as honey, so they are called slaves of lust."

Gradually, this girl became jealous of the queen, so she denigrated and incited the king to have people use bows and arrows to shoot at the queen. Who would have thought that all the arrows shot would fly around her three times and then return and fall in front of the king. King Up-dien was frightened, knowing that he was at fault, he immediately went to the Buddha to ask for repentance. On that occasion, the Buddha taught King Up-dien the words in this passage.

tieu_de: Do not incite people to litigate
noi_dung:
DO NOT INDUCE PEOPLE IN LITIGATION

Explanation

Disputation and litigation have different meanings each other. Arguing means only using words to argue right and wrong, while chanting means using single words, bringing each other to the front door to confront, asking for arbitration. From ancient times until now, people who are good at fighting must sometimes die from fighting, and people who like to litigate must sometimes fail miserably in litigation. One mistake would mean the family fortune would be ruined, like a moth rushing into a fire, even if one wanted to repent, there would be no time left.

Considering the cause of the lawsuit, it's basically no more than two things: if it weren't for fighting over fields, houses, property and money, it would have been due to fighting and conflict. Those who fight for property, of course, are all greedy for money, but they don't know that once they get involved in filing a lawsuit to the customs,

you can't help but spend all your money. Of course, people who are involved in fighting and conflict value face, but they do not know that once they go to the court and accept others to judge, it will be impossible to save face.

The person who lost the lawsuit of course had to shake his head, but the person who won the lawsuit certainly couldn't help but feel a shock. Only when the house is broken, do you regret that you didn't patiently tolerate the other person's stubbornness in the first place. How about being able to calmly sit down with the other person and discuss all the reasonable things before the incident happens, and discuss and find a solution without having to rely on lawsuits?

A person who can be patient, tolerant and forgiving is a wise person; If you still incite others to litigate, you are definitely not a good person. If it weren't for wanting to profit from the dispute between the two sides, it would be someone who wants to use public affairs to take private revenge, using a knife to kill people. Only when the wind calms down do we clearly see the other person's evil intentions, why don't we feel sorry for ourselves for being a petty person and hurting our own virtue?

Citing the story

MANY LIVES WITHOUT SUE1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Su Co Bien (師古編). (Author's note)

During the Northern Song Dynasty,2 there was Loi Phu who was from Nghi district

NOTE 2

The An Si Complete Book wrote it as the Tang Dynasty, mistakenly, because Loi Phu lived in the Northern Song Dynasty, his ancestor Loi Hoanh lived in the Tang Dynasty. Road.

Feng belongs to Jiangxi province, has a naturally benevolent nature, and has never been stubborn and conflicted with anyone. Since the generation of his ancestors, 1 has always passed down his loyalty to his children. Up to eleven generations of Loi Phu, there has never been a lawsuit against another person.

NOTE 1

According to the book of Nhan genea (人譜) recorded, Loi Phu's ancestor was Mr. Loi Hoanh, who lived during his lifetime. Tang Dynasty.

Later, Loi Phu passed the PhD exam, became an honest mandarin, and later rose to the position of Grand Master teaching the crown prince. Everyone believes that it is thanks to his ancestors who accumulated many good deeds.

Comment

If you cannot be tolerant and forgive others, you must first practice patience. By persistently maintaining patience over a long period of time, one's mind is naturally open and one can become tolerant.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Ta Cau who hated litigation. Neighbors encroached on his land, someone advised him to sue the mandarin. Ta Cau smiled and said: "He can only take over land, how can he take over heaven?" After that, there was no need to argue. How can small-minded people understand those words?

WISDOM AVOIDS DISASTER2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book Gong Too Way (功過格). (Editor's note)

In a certain village, Hoa Chau district, Anhui province, there was a person raising hundreds of geese. One day, geese came to eat a neighbor's rice, and more than fifty of them were beaten to death at once. Goose farmer's wife

At first I was very angry when I saw that, but then I calmed down and thought: "If we bring this matter to the court, our family's power is unlikely to win the case; if we want to win the case, we will have to spend a lot of money. Moreover, our husband is drunk, if he hears about this, it will definitely cause a fight and an unpredictable disaster. Let's just be patient and let it go." Immediately told the family to hide the goose's carcass and not let her husband know.

Early the next morning, the neighbor who killed the goose suddenly fell dead. After the husband sobered up, he told his wife: "If I had known about the death of the goose yesterday, while drunk, I wouldn't have been able to help but go to their house and start a fight. Today I would have brought disaster and ruined the house."

Discussion

When people are extremely angry, if they can take a step back to calmly think, they can preserve their body, family, life, and even eliminate the afflictions of injustice. Looking at the patience of the goose farmer's wife, doesn't that preserve a lot? In the past, Pham Van Chinh Cong once wrote a poem of advice to life:

心中忿怒不如休，
何須經縣又經州？
縱然費盡千般計，
贏得貓來輸去牛。

The heart is angry and restless,
Ha tu Kinh district Huu Kinh Chau?
Suddenly waste all the plans of the sky,
Dou Dac Meo will take over the cow.

Translation:

In anger, it is best to restrain yourself.
There is no need to file a lawsuit to the district or continent?
For example, if you add up hundreds of thousands of expenses,
It turns out that if you get the cat, you will lose the buffalo!

Poem translation:

The fire of anger that flares up must be extinguished immediately,
Sue the government or district. What's good?
If you win the case, cover the costs,
Lost a buffalo, gain a plowshare!

A LADY MUST DIE YOUNG1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Heavenly Induction (感應篇). (Author's note)

Ha Ung Nguyen was a clerk in To Chau prefecture and gave birth to a son named Than. When Than was just 4 years old, his nanny took him to visit his grandfather's house. On the way past Lang Gia mountain, when it was almost dawn, I suddenly saw a group of people with lights and torches coming. When they met Ha Than, they looked scared and moved aside and said: "Is Young Master Ha here? We should go away." After saying that, everyone went another way.

The nanny came home and told the story. Ha Ung Nguyen thought that this child would eventually become a noble person.

But then when Ha Than was 17 years old, he suddenly became blind in both eyes. Ung Nguyen was very sad and angry. He heard that there was a Taoist monk in Truc Duong who could summon gods, so he came to ask. The divine apparition said: "Your son should have passed the exam, only because when he was a clerk he accepted bribes from people, fabricated evidence, harmed many innocent people and had to be imprisoned, so God forced him to renounce his family. This son will be reborn in another house with good fortune."

Sure enough, not long after, Ha Than died.

Discussion

Because previous lives had a predestined relationship with each other, we were born as descendants. Among those who have predestined relationships, there are also good people and stupid people, all of which are brought on by people themselves. Alas, just because of greed and fabrication of evidence, we killed a child with a brilliant future. How pitiful!

tieu_de: Do not destroy the fame and fortune of others
noi_dung:
DO NOT RUIN THE WAY FAME OF OTHERS

Explain widely

Reputation is the part that fully represents the identity and career of each person. personal; profit is a resource that helps people get food and clothing as well as everything needed in daily life. Each person's reputation is difficult to build, but it is very easy and quick to destroy it. If there are times when you want to destroy someone else's career, you should think back to the hardships they had to go through to build it, so would you have the heart to destroy it?

Like a person throwing ashes against the wind, common sense will dirty itself; If you raise your face to the sky and spit, you will surely fall back down and dirty your face; These things are all natural. Therefore, destroying someone else's reputation inevitably damages your own dignity, and destroying someone else's resources is also silently destroying your own blessings and virtues.

Citing the story

ENTERING TO EXAMINATION SCHOOL TO COLLECT OLD DEBT1

After all, when the three calamities of the final life stage arise, the branches and leaves of trees turn into sharp knives, people who touch them are immediately injured, but no one can avoid that calamity. Like when the World-Honored One suffered from a wooden spear piercing his foot, that wooden stick was only one meter long but could penetrate a large green stone, and followed the Buddha from one place to another, wouldn't that be even more trustworthy?1

tieu_de: Don't break up people's marriages
noi_dung:
DO NOT DISRUPT PEOPLE'S MARRIAGE
Person

Expounding

In the meaning of the two words marriage (婚姻), a boy who marries is called kn (婚), a girl who marries her husband is called nhan (姻). The word kôn (婚) is originally taken from the meaning of kôn (昏) which means dark night, because in the past, the main part of this ceremony was that the ceremony was only performed at night, not during the day, which implied shame. The word ren (姻) is taken from the meaning of ren ren (因人), which means to rely on people, meaning that once a girl has followed her husband, she must wholeheartedly maintain harmony, rely on her husband to maintain morality

morality, and also rely on her husband to entrust the happiness, humiliation, and suffering of her whole life, which means that the wife is always dependent on her husband.

Marriage is a beautiful union between two families, first inheriting the career of the ancestors of the family, then building and expanding for future descendants, and now connecting in harmony with the relatives of both sides, it is truly a great fate.

In general, marriage is inherently determined by predestined relationships in previous lives. Not only do we ourselves not have the ability to take the initiative, but even the parents of both sides are not able to proactively decide. If it is brought about by good causes and conditions, the thoughts of good harmony will continue without end. If it is caused by evil causes, the toxic resentment will continue forever.

Therefore, marriage does not have to be destroyed by human force. For example, if a person wants to destroy something, if it is not someone who harbors hatred, then it must be because of jealousy. Regardless of whether the mind has not been destroyed yet, or when it has already been destroyed, the crime is considered to have been committed.

Intentionally sabotaging someone's marriage is of course not advisable. But even labeling other people as husband and wife cannot be without caution. For example, if the age difference is too far, we cannot live together until our teeth turn gray; Or we should not underestimate factors such as the difference between luxury and lowliness, and not being able to register for each other. Until

things such as rich and poor family background, ugly and beautiful image are not out of consideration.

Citing stories

KNOWING ERRORS CORRECTING ERRORS1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Ton Thi Lang's memoirs (孫侍郎記事). (Author's note)

Quan Thi lang Ton Hong, when he was young, he had a friend who studied at a Thai school far away from home. The two of them had an agreement that when a letter arrived from home, they would show it to each other. One day, his friend received a letter from home but hid it from Ton Hong. After Ton Hong learned and asked, his friend said: "There are random things in the letter, I'm afraid it will discourage you." Ton Hong still tried to see it until he could, but in the end the friend had to show his father's letter. In the letter, it was written: "Last night, I dreamed of going to a mandarin's palace. I dreamed that I was looking through the book recording the names of those who passed the exam. In it, I saw the name of my son with Ton Hong, but Ton Hong's name was written down at the bottom, and there was a line of red letters that said: 'On that day, month, year... wrote for a person by that name... a divorce petition, so I was punished by heaven and had my name taken away from the book.'"

Ton Hong read the letter and looked very surprised, his friend immediately asked: "Is there such a thing?" Ton Hong replied: "That was a long time ago. When I was in a certain continent..., I met an elderly couple, yelling at each other, wanting a divorce, but no one could write a petition for me. Then they asked me to write a petition, I had absolutely no bad intentions." The friend comforted him: "The dream story is not accurate, there is no need to pay attention. Moreover, if you are talented in studying, how could you not pass the exam?"

At the exam, that classmate passed the exam, Ton Hong was indeed failed. From then on, I realized that the dream I had the day before was not an illusion. Seeing that Ton Hong was unhappy about that incident, his friend immediately said: "Don't be sad anymore. When I return to my hometown, I will replace you and persuade the couple to reunite like before, okay?" Having said that, he asked carefully about the names and whereabouts of the other two people, then went to the place and saw that they had not reunited, so he told Ton Hong's story to them all, and then arranged a party to persuade them to reunite like before. When the matter was accomplished, he immediately sent a letter to Ton Hong. Ton Hong was extremely grateful and happy.

Later, Ton Hong was exempted from the provincial exam because he was a boarding student at the Thai Hoc school. He gradually became a high-ranking mandarin and held positions in large districts many times. Wherever he went, when he met a family that wanted a divorce, he tried his best to reconcile, thereby protecting the happiness of many families.

Commentary

In the last year of the Southern Song Dynasty,1 in Lam Xuyen, there was a person named Vuong, whose wife Luong Thi was captured by the Yuan invaders, resisted and died. After many years, the husband planned to remarry but always encountered difficulties and failed. One night, I dreamed that my wife appeared

NOTE 1

That was the year 1279.

said: "I was born in that house, now I am ten years old, in seven years I will be your wife." The next day, he immediately sent someone to look for him according to the dream. Sure enough, he found him, so he waited seven years to bring a gift to ask for her hand in marriage. Just once was enough. Therefore, the relationship between husband and wife cannot be taken lightly and destroyed?

MARRIAGE DISSOLUTION MUST Suffer Retribution1

Excerpted from the book Khuyen cheng luc (勸懲錄). (Author's note)

During the Qing Dynasty, the year of Thuan Tri, in the year of Mau Tuat2, the Hoi Exam Department was opened. During roll call, I suddenly discovered that in the pen holder of a contestant from Hieu Liem3 there was a draft of a divorce petition. The judge was very angry when he saw it, so he used a staff to beat him, then shackled him and locked him in prison, and immediately stripped him of his bachelor's status.4

Belongs to Thuong district South, Zhejiang province.

Next, when the couple separated, they immediately set up a marriage match with the other person, and wrote a divorce petition for this person. This guy's plan is truly extremely sinister! You should know that in the law of heaven, destroying another person's marriage is considered the most evil thing. Not only should you not easily talk about divorce after becoming husband and wife, but even if you are not married, if things have already been decided, you cannot change them.

In my hometown in Con Son, there was a family that was formerly a famous family and had only one daughter. After so many years, the master felt grateful for the servant's heart, immediately returned this man's previous prostitution contract, and treated him respectfully as a friend.

That servant had a very intelligent and handsome son, whom the master wanted to marry. The servant tried his best to refuse, not daring to, but after the master forced him too much, he had to obey and let the two children become husband and wife, living together very compatible.

Not long after, both the master and his wife passed away, and the servant immediately took care of and raised his daughter-in-law. The next year, someone from the old owner's clan, using the excuse that the two sides of the family were so far apart that they could not get married, tried to find ways to harass them incessantly, and finally sued the mandarin. The judge judges both sides

divorced, the last servant lost his family because of it. The old owner's clan members were unable to care for their daughter, so in the end she had to starve, suffer, and die. Not long after that girl died, she merged with her former owner's clan and told the whole story. Many of the co-conspirators in this case all later became seriously ill and died one after another.

tieu_de: It is not because of personal hatred that causes discord among brothers and sisters
noi_dung:
NOT FOR OWN RESULTS
MAKE BROTHERS OTHERS DISCONDITION

Preach widely

Brothers in one family, although their physical appearance is different, their temperament is similar because they were born to the same parents. Although they are different in age, they are all raised by their parents. If siblings do not get along, they are sinning against their parents. Therefore, if you cause discord between other brothers and sisters, it means making them sin against their parents.

With brothers from different fathers, even though the lineage is the same, we still have the same father, like limbs that are interdependent, if we do not get along with each other, it is ill-treating our own flesh and blood. Therefore, if you cause discord with another person's half-siblings, it means causing them to mistreat their relatives.

Brothers and relatives in the family, although distinct from each other, rely on the ancestors' virtue to protect and nurture them. If they do not get along with each other, it is clearly disrespectful to their ancestors. Therefore, if you cause discord among other people's relatives, it means making them disrespect their ancestors.

So we must know that private revenge is extremely small, but the future harm of discord is extremely great. If someone truly respects their parents and treats their brothers well, then they can use their love for their brothers to understand the brotherhood of others. So how can they be cruel because of their own revenge and make others unkind to their younger siblings and disrespectful to their brothers?

Citing stories

THANH HOANG QU RESPONSE1

NOTE 1

belong to Shanghai today.

After death, all three people found themselves being led to the Tutelary God temple. all have clear, error-free records? Therefore, there are still injustices in the earthly world, but the underworld absolutely does not judge wrongly. On earth there is also the influence of emotions when judging, but in the underworld it only follows the law. The questioning of sins in the earthly world is only judged according to the things in this life, but the impeachment of the underworld considers everything in many previous lives. People who encounter injustice, if they clearly understand the fate of previous lives, the resentment will disappear.

I remember in the year of Nham Tuat,1 in Nam Tuong town, also in the Gia Dinh region, in Luc Chan Cau's family, a very strange thing happened. According to that family member, the ghosts of the underworld must have written messages when traveling, and2 are not allowed to cross river wharves.

That year, Luc Chan Cau's niece-in-law was sick, suddenly a demon possessed him, and said to himself: "I was originally from Vu Nguyen district, Huy Chau, on the northern river bank selling fish eggs. The officials said there was nothing to complain about, and immediately showed me a copy of it. It contained all the debts that I owed to that person in my previous life. Once I learned it, I was no longer angry. The underworld official immediately gave me a letter, telling me to return home. But when I passed by, his servant splashed water on the letter and made it dirty, so I can't return the letter quickly.

Luc Chan Cau said: "The message is from the underworld, I know how to replace it, so go back to the place where it was issued and ask for a new one."

The ghost said: "I have come here, in front is the citadel, behind is the guard station, even if I want to go back, I can't go back."

Luc Chan Cau immediately asked: "So what should I do?"

The ghost said: "In this area there is a person with that last name, in that village... who can help with this."
