Luc Chan Cau immediately took him to the door, and the ghost immediately came out and disappeared. Chan Cau's niece-in-law then gradually recovered from her illness.

Who dares to say that yin and yang are two different paths, different reasons?

tieu_de: Don't let other people's fathers and children fall into conflict because of small interests
noi_dung:
NOT FOR SMALL PROFITS MAKE OTHER PERSONS AND CHILDREN
INTO CONFLICT

Preach widely

The religion of father and son is inherently heavy. more than brotherly love. Sibling discord in a family is a bad thing, against morality, but if father and son separate from each other, they will lose the way of heaven. Imagine if an outsider, for their own benefit, instigated our father and son to separate, causing conflicts between our flesh and blood? Feel sorry for your parents, look back at your children and grandchildren with compassion; looking after children and grandchildren, admiring their ancestors and suffering; Is it cruel to do that? Based on what argument can you do that?

Therefore, the sages of ancient times have always taught that: If you respect your own ancestors, you must know how to respect other people's ancestors; If you love your own children, you must know how to love other people's children. Therefore, we must ensure that everyone at home respects their parents, where all elders live long and enjoy blessings, only then will our heart to take care of our parents be complete, and our wish to educate our children will be at peace. If that is not the case, if we look closely, we cannot help but become unfilial to our parents and irresponsible to our children and grandchildren.

When it comes to discord, there are many reasons

causes. If it weren't for the exchange of words, it would be because it was related to money and property; If it weren't for the parents' unfair bias towards their children, then it would have been because of the same bloodline that the two brothers were the same, giving rise to bias from one side to the other... However, considering the ultimate root cause, the word "benefit" cannot be left out in the teachings of Emperor Quan.

The reason why we say "small benefits" doesn't necessarily refer to trivial and trivial things, but what we mean is that even comparing things like houses, fields, and gardens with the discord between father and son, we must see that all of those material values ​​are trivial. If you cling to words and do not understand the profound meaning of such words, you will inevitably violate the teachings of Emperor Quan.

Citing stories

Leding other people's lives will result in a ruined house1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Dan Guixi (丹桂籍). (Author's note)

There was a rich man named Tu Tri, who lived next to Tu Bat's house. Seeing Tu Bat's large and beautiful house, Tu Tri immediately had the ambition to find a way to appropriate it as his own. But Tu Bat has absolutely no intention of selling the house. Tu Tri immediately plotted to lure Tu Bat's child into gambling, gradually spoiling his passion, destroying his family's fortune, and eventually forcing Tu Bat to sell his house to Tu Tri.

Tu Bat had a lot of hatred in his heart, so father and son were at odds. Tu Bat was sad and angry and died. Not long after, Tu Tri had three children and five grandchildren who were all seriously ill. Tu Tri dreamed that his grandfather appeared and said: "Disaster is coming. Do you remember, not long after you bought the house, Tu Bat died. He sued you in the underworld."

Tu Tri woke up very scared, so he immediately went to pray for the island at the Thanh Hoang temple. When I first entered the temple, I suddenly saw a beggar looking very surprised, so I asked him why. The other person replied: "Yesterday, I happened to be sleeping in front of the temple. I saw a person holding a lawsuit in his hand, saying he was suing Tu Tri for seducing his son into spoiling his family. I didn't expect that Tu Tri himself would come here to offer sacrifices, so I was surprised."

Tu Tri heard that and was even more afraid. Before that year was over, he became bedridden and died.

Discussion

Because you covet someone else's house, you devise a plan to destroy the relationship between father and son, causing them to separate from each other, causing them to have their home broken up, which is truly a malicious thought.

In the past, there was a Minister of the Zhao family from Giang You, whose house was close to a Provincial Yuan1 of the

NOTE 1

Provincial Yuan (省元), also called Tinh Hui (魁), was a title from the Song Dynasty used to refer to a Doctor who passed the exam organized by the Ministry of Rites. Because the Ministry of Rites belongs to the Provincial Minister (尚書省), the person who passes first is called Provincial Nguyen.

Thuong. The Thuong family has a beautiful landscape garden, which Minister Trieu wants to use his power to take over. The Thuong family secretly knew, so they wrote a poem and sent it to Minister Trieu, along with the garden's title documents. The content of the poem is as follows:

The vastness of heaven and earth has parts,
Cunning plots are not easy to distinguish.
The door of the peach blossom cave welcomes Qin guests.
That garden is the owner, the body is the guest,
How long do you have left?

Minister Trieu read the poem and immediately sent back the title documents, not daring to accept it. Compared to Tu Tri, it can be said that he woke up early, understood the problem, and turned disaster into blessing.

tieu_de: Don't rely on power to humiliate good people
noi_dung:
DON'T BASE ON POWER HUMILATE THE GOOD

Preach widely

When you have power, of course it is easy to become eminent, but then again It's also very easy to lose. During the time of great fame, there must be servants and servants crowded together in the house, there is no shortage of flatterers, no matter what you say casually, everyone will listen carefully. When the situation falls, those close to you turn away, those who were once grateful are now enemies, then even if you speak with all your heart, people will ignore you as if they didn't listen. They are the same person, but sometimes they are enthusiastic, sometimes they are indifferent and cold, life is always like that.

So you must know that when you have power in your hands, you should not rely on it, let alone rely on the power of others? What's more, let's rely on that to humiliate good people?

To humiliate a good person is a sin, but to rely on power to humiliate a good person is a crime on top of a crime. The rich have power, the rich also have power; Those who work as mandarins have power, and the clerks who help the mandarins also have power. Although those powers are different, the mindset of the person who wants to rely on them must be the same. When you think you can rely on power, you naturally want to humiliate others.

Speaking of “gentleness”, gentleness is gentle and kind, which is the opposite quality of evil; and salary is pure honesty, to distinguish it from despicable deceit and deceit. Both kindness and honesty are qualities that should not be humiliated, even when meeting a truly kind person, the thought of humiliating should not arise. Therefore, if you rely on power to humiliate good people, that sin is much worse than humiliating others.

Citing stories

WANT TO BE PROMOTED WHICH HURTS PEOPLE1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Mingxiangji (冥祥記). (Author's note)

During the Northern and Southern dynasties, the Liang dynasty, there was a man named Hoanh in Khuc A,2 who was extremely wealthy and often went to Tuong Chau to trade wood. After several years of trading, I was able to buy several large logs of wood, more than 50 meters long, which is truly rare. At that time, Emperor Wu3 wanted to build Hoang Co Pagoda above the tomb of Emperor Van4 so he sought to buy precious wood. At that time, Hoanh's wood was being transported to Nam Tan. The chief officer of Nam Tan, Manh Thieu Khanh, because he wanted the court to issue a decree to promote him, so he thought of a plan to gain merit by searching the Hoanh family's clothes and belongings, then falsely accusing them of being stolen, saying that the Hoanh family's wood was longer than traditional regulations and was not commercial wood, so they confiscated everything and put it in the warehouse, submitted it to the Vo De to use to build a pagoda, and also sentenced the Hoanh family to death.

NOTE 2

Now is Danyang County in Jiangsu Province.

On the day of his execution, they Hoanh told his wife and children to fill his coffin with all kinds of yellow paper and pens. The Hoanh family told them to write Manh Thieu's full name

Khanh on dozens of pieces of paper and then swallow them all.

How sad! The blessings of sentient beings in the time of decline gradually decrease, and natural products become increasingly poorer. In general, the poorer people are, the faster the forests are severely cut down, not to mention the fact that the land is becoming more and more degraded and less fertile. During the Sui Tang dynasty and before, most of the rice flowers were more than a meter long,2 vegetables and fruits were all delicious, flowers and grass were fragrant, but

CATCHING THE DOG TO WITNESS1

Lieu Thang, from Binh Chi, from Mao Kim village, incompetent but somehow abused a small official position, relied on others to bully people regardless of morality, had a greedy and cruel nature, only tried to find ways to make a lot of money, even though he was not merciful towards relatives. The district commander of that area, An Thuat Khanh, was also greedy and cruel. The two colluded together to do all kinds of bad things. When they earned money, they shared it together. Those who were harmed by them all mourned in pain and prayed and denounced the gods.

Not even half a year had passed when Lieu Thang suddenly fell down and died miserably. At the time of death, his eyes, ears, nose, and mouth were all bleeding. Just a few days later, An Thuat Khanh also became seriously ill and died. While waiting for burial, his body suddenly became full of maggots. On the same day, Lieu Thang's old servant and the dog in the house also died. Khanh, both were beaten with whips so fiercely that I couldn't bear to look. The King of Hell sent me a piece of paper, in which was written the amount of money I had paid before. replaced the boss to receive people's money, and the black dog, who usually followed me every time I went to receive money, had both me and the dog arrested to testify. A moment later, on the throne there was a shout: 'Liu Thang, An Thuat Khanh, banish them all to hell, this crime will never be pardoned.' Discussion

The An family rules the district, spreading crime everywhere, destroying countless people, not to mention having the Lieu family under their hands, helping cruel people do tyrannical things? Retribution to hell is of course unavoidable.

Thinking so, he immediately sent his son Thanh Thoi to take his business card to give it to the government official, hoping to intervene. The government sent people to go with Thanh Thoi, arrested Trieu Tho in front of the public hall, and punished him with a staff.

Khau Manh Hoa immediately comforted Trau Tho: "You are dead, you can't come back to life, let me set up a repentance altar to pray for you."

Hon Trau Tho said: "The matter has been brought to Dong Nhac, I can't do anything anymore. I will question him today, of course he must go there with me."

Sure enough, before that day was over, Thanh Thoi died.

tieu_de: Don't rely on wealth and look down on poor people
noi_dung:
DON'T ATTEND THE RICH TO THE CHEAP
THE WORSE PEOPLE

Teach widely

Be rich or miserable are both rich and poor. There are causes and conditions, although there are differences, they are all due to what each person has done in their previous lives. But judging from the current situation, the happiness and suffering of the poor and the rich are clearly worlds apart.

People who live in a wealthy and wealthy environment should always maintain a loyal heart, often be careful to guard against dangerous times, always respectfully and cautiously follow morality, and in everything they do, they must know how to love and think of the poor and miserable, only then can they increase their own blessings.

On the contrary, if you see a person in a dire situation, unable to protect themselves, easily disrespectful, then immediately oppress, oppress, chase away, humiliate or mistreat, or use cunning tricks to force them to do what they want, or use usury to exploit them, what kind of retribution they will have to face later can be easily known, there is no need to say.

You should know, money Inheritance is something that comes and goes with no certainty. Today the garden is deserted,

next year it will become a bustling nightclub, so who can be sure that the rich will not at some point become miserable and empty-handed? Wouldn't it be much better if we had learned to follow kindness earlier? Rich and wealthy people always want to keep their wealth and prosperity forever, but unfortunately they often sow the cause of misery. That disaster originally came from not knowing cause and effect, forgetting one's own ancient nature.

The Sutra of Similes1 teaches: "A wise person thinks about material wealth, knowing that it cannot be kept for long. For example, a house is on fire, a wise person clearly knows the destructive power of fire, so before the fire has started, he hastily takes all the assets out of the house. Therefore, although the house burns down, the assets are fully preserved, then rebuild the house, expanding the business. A wise person cultivates blessings. Virtue and diligence in almsgiving are the same...2 Stupid people, when they see their house on fire, only feel regret for the house, struggling to find ways to put out the fire, not knowing the destructive power of the fire, so not only the house cannot be saved, but their assets are also gone. The greedy and deceitful person who does not know how to practice almsgiving is the same..."

NOTE 1

Actually, this passage is taken verbatim from the Collection of Sutras and Examples (眾經撰雜譬喻), included in the Dai Chanh new revision of the Tripitaka in volume 4, sutra number 208, a total of two volumes, compiled by Mr. Dao Luoc, translated by Mr. Kumarajiva in the Dao Qin Dynasty. This excerpt starts from line 10, page 531, sheet b, of volume 1.

NOTE 2

Here, the author has omitted a passage from the scriptures.

So know that not disdaining the needy is also knowing how to preserve one's own wealth.

Citing facts

DO NOT PRESS THE POOR1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Induction of Divine Mantra (感應篇註證). (Author's note)

Macheng district, Hubei province, there was a mandarin who had accumulated thousands of taels of silver in assets, preparing to redeem the land he had sold 20 years earlier.

The son in the family had just turned 12 years old. When he heard about it, he immediately asked his father: "The people who bought our fields before, how many families were there in total?" The father said: "About more than twenty houses." The son asked again: "Those families bought their fields, how much did it cost to repair and build them?" The father immediately calculated all the expenses and told his son.

At that time, the son calmly said: "So, if we redeem it at the previous selling price, those families will have to suffer a lot.2 If our family can redeem the field, it will also suffer negative morals. Moreover, if our family has money, why worry about not having a field, why do we need to fight for the fields that are supporting more than twenty families? Furthermore, it is very difficult for those poor families to buy fields. It's difficult, but my family wants to buy the field back easily. For example, they receive their money back at the previous price, but now they can only buy the field

NOTE 2

From this, we can deduce that in the previous contract of sale, there must have been an agreement that the seller of the field could later redeem it at the price it was sold for

half of the area, not to mention how easy it is for poor families to have money in their hands without losing more or less?”

The father thought for a long time and then said: "What you said is very reasonable, but there are 18 acres of fields near my grandparents' graves that must be redeemed to be used for offerings and grave cleaning. Otherwise, I will not redeem them anymore."

The son said again: "If it must be so, you should buy it at the current price, not necessarily redeem it."

The father did as his son said. Therefore, those who owned fields were very grateful for that favor, often going to the Manh Tuong shrine in the village to pray for gods to protect their benefactor.

When that son was 18 years old, he passed the exams consecutively, so he was promoted to the position of Governor of Nghiem Chau. One day, he was riding his horse across the bridge when the horse suddenly became nervous and jumped into the river. At that critical moment, suddenly the Strong General appeared in the air, reached out his hand to support him, and sat him down neatly on the edge of the bridge. That's when I realized that people had been praying for him for a long time. It really had an impact. Later, that son lived to be over 80 years old.

Discussion

According to the contract, redeeming the field is completely legitimate and does not seem to cause harm to others. But a child of that

age, who can consider and see the hidden things inside things, is truly worthy of respect from both gods and humans, and has abundant blessings and longevity.

INITIATION OF COMPASSION1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Gong Too Way (功過格). (Author's note)

Mai Gong is from Xiangzhou, Hunan province, and was formerly the district commander of Gu'an. One day, an internal affairs officer brought a pig's trotter to Mai Cong, asking for help with a debt. The public servant had the pig's trotters cooked, invited the eunuch to come and drink with him, and then called the debtor to scold him. The other person argued that it was because the family was so poor. Cong Mai shouted: "If you owe a debt to a noble person, do you dare to beg for poverty? You must pay today, if you delay, I will punish you to death."

The debtor cried and retreated. The civil warden seemed a little moved by compassion. Cong Mai immediately called the other man back and said sadly: "Honestly, I know you are very poor, but there is no other way. Go home quickly, sell your wife and children, then bring the money here to pay the mandarin. Only, I am an official and a parent, like the parents of the people, I really cannot bear to cause your family to be torn apart, I will be slow to give it to you." One day, you'll go back and say goodbye to your wife and children. It's like we'll never see each other again in this life."

Mai Cong mentioned this and the debtor was so heartbroken that he cried. Princess Mai also cried, the mandarin

jai also burst into tears, immediately stopped collecting debts, and later canceled the debt papers.

Later, Cong Mai became an official to the position of Thi Lang, his career became even more glorious.

Discussion

Mai Cong did not bend herself to do as the internal warden asked for help, but it did not hurt his feelings, and was able to change a secretly greedy heart. The essential key to doing all of that is to arouse compassion in the human conscience.

tieu_de: Close to good people, stay away from bad people
noi_dung:
Close to good people,
STAY AWAY from evil people

Preach widely

Dijun taught that: “ When you meet good people, you must Be close and close to yourself, because it can help you increase the goodness of your mind and the goodness of your body. If you encounter bad or evil people, you must stay away immediately, because in just a blink of an eye, they can bring us unimaginable disasters." Good and bad people are clearly divided; When it comes to taste, it's like the fragrant sage grass and the smelly elm grass; Talking about dignity is like the noble phoenix and the hateful owl. That's why it's said: “Close to ink, it's black, close to light, it's bright.” That's a very natural argument.

Being close and close to good people, their noble and pure virtues will have the effect of molding and cultivating ourselves. If we stay away from and avoid evil people, the disasters caused by that person will not have anything to rely on to cause harm to us. From the gods to the common people, from ancient times, everyone has considered being close to good people and far away from evil people to be of the utmost importance. That's because through consideration, we always see that the impacts and influences of surrounding circumstances often silently change people's personalities and emotions.

Good people do not always do good deeds, but in every moment of thinking, speaking, and acting, if they recognize evil, they immediately stay away from it. Evil people do not always do evil things, but in every moment of thinking, speaking, and doing, if they recognize good things, they will naturally avoid them.

For example, if I want to do a good deed, help a poor person, save a life, if a good person sees and knows that, he will find every way to approve and support it, because he thinks that doing it will definitely bring blessings, but an evil person, seeing that, will find all kinds of ways to prevent it, because he thinks it is a useless fantasy.

The person who advises has conscientiously given all the warnings, can it be that the person who listens but don't try your best to follow through? As far as I know, there are many people who, thanks to good surrounding circumstances, have changed for the better. Mencius's mother moved three times to teach her son, for fear that her son would learn bad things. Even the saints and sages are like that, let alone ordinary people?

And it's not just humans, it's the same for all species. Once upon a time, in the country of Hoa Thi there was a white elephant with the power to destroy enemies. When people in the country committed crimes and died, the king immediately ordered them to be put in cages and trampled to death by elephants. Later, the elephant's stable burned down, so people moved it to a new place, near a temple. The elephant heard the monk in the temple chanting the Dhammapada, and when he heard the sentence "Doing good will lead to heaven, doing evil will go to hell", he looked frightened, as if he had some understanding. From then on, when people brought sinners, the elephants no longer crushed them to death, they only used their trunks to smell them and stuck out their tongues to lick them. The king knew about it and immediately brought the elephant to live near the slaughterhouse. Elephants often see scenes of killing, and their evil hearts flare up like before.

So, isn't the influence of what you see and hear very important? When you meet a kind person, not only should you be close to yourself, but you should also teach your children to be close. Not only do we advise our children to be close and close, but for all those who are close or familiar, whenever we have the opportunity to talk, we should advise them to be close to that kind person. On the contrary, if you see evil people, you must not only avoid and stay away from them, but also advise your children to stay away. Not only do we advise our children to stay away, but for all those who are close or acquainted, if we have the opportunity to say an honest word, we should advise them to stay away from that person.

Why is that? Because the two paths of good and evil do not follow the same direction and cannot go together. If you cannot

get close to a gentleman, you will have to be close to a petty person. Good people are easily drawn to the evil path, but evil people find it very difficult to transform to the good path.

I often see people from small villages gathering all day long, talking haphazardly; Some people get drunk and become violent, leading to the destruction of their homes and their lives; Some people like to use force and cause quarrels and fights, which also leads to family destruction and loss of life; There are people who are immersed in gambling and infatuated with prostitutes, and their homes are ruined and their lives are gone. Looking closely at these self-inflicted disasters and causing so much harm, the initial cause only arose from a few people unanimously agreeing, in a moment of excitement, doing bad things, then others gradually followed suit, completely unexpected that the later disaster could be so terrible. tieu_de: Roads that have been bumpy for many years need to be repaired and leveled

Broadening

If today it can be repaired and leveled, then from now on, for many years to come, every day will be convenient for countless people to travel.

Among those countless people, there are people who can travel conveniently on days of heavy rain and wind, there are people who can travel conveniently carrying heavy luggage, and there are people who can travel conveniently in the afternoon and evening. In silence, the horrors of countless old people and children were erased; and also secretly reduce the number of falls for countless blind and handicapped people. Isn't such a great contribution?

Saying "bumpy roads" is only talking about roads. If this idea is expanded, then clogged rivers, winding streams, all of which are obstacles for boats and boats when moving, can also be considered "bumpy roads". The way to repair in these

cases is to make it easier to travel, to think of ways to dredge, clear the flow, repair difficult places, helping future generations to enjoy that grace forever. Doing so means contributing to repairing and leveling "bumpy roads" that have been there for many years.

Mr. Hu Giang's father was Mr. Nam Loc, his ancestor many generations ago was a student of the famous artist Phuong Hieu Nho,1 due to being involved in the case of the teacher2 had to move to Duong Pho in Truong Chau, since then his descendants have lived on farming profession, with outsiders he never dared to discuss literature and books.

Sometimes when we see a good deed, we do it but we're not really determined or strong, or sometimes we do something to help others but in our hearts we often doubt [the result], or sometimes we try to follow the good deed but our words are wrong, or when we're sober we try our best to maintain morality, but when we drink alcohol we're often indulgent and indulgent. Every day I consider my mistakes and subtract them from the good deeds I have done. Some days I eliminate them all and have nothing left. So from the year of the Snake2, one vows to do good deeds, but it is not until the year of the Cat,3, after more than 10 years, that the full number of 3,000 good deeds is completed.

NOTE 3

Every good deed I did was written down. My wife is illiterate, so every time she does a good deed, she uses a quill to dip in red ink and prints it on that day's calendar as a round dot, usually good deeds like donating food to the poor, or buying live animals to release animals... On days when she does a lot, there are sometimes more than ten dots like that. By August of the Year of the Goat1, 3,000 good deeds are enough. On September 13 of that year, I again made a wish to pass the doctoral exam, vowing to do 10,000 good deeds.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1583.

In the year of Binh Tuat2 I passed the doctorate exam and was appointed as Tri of Bao De district. I prepared a blank notebook, named it Tri Tam notebook. Early in the morning when I left for work, I told my family to give that notebook to the translation office to put on my desk. Every action of the day was divided into good and bad, meticulously recorded in that notebook, every night an incense burner was placed in front of the yard, following the example of Trieu Duyet Dao in the past, reporting everything to God.3

NOTE 3

My wife saw that there were not many good deeds recorded, so she frowned and said: "Before, when you were still at home, I could help you do good deeds, so the number of 3,000 good deeds was completed. That night, I dreamed that I suddenly met a god, and immediately presented the difficult task of doing enough good deeds to the god. The god said: "Just reducing the land tax for the people, ten thousand good deeds are enough."

Originally, the land in Bao De district [previously] had to pay a tax of 2 centimeters 3 cups 7 dimes per acre,1 [when I took office] I reconsidered, reducing it to 1 centimeter 4 cups 6 dimes. There is indeed such a thing, but I still have some doubts in my heart, [not thinking that it would have such a great effect]. Luckily, at that time, Zen Master Huyen Du came from Ngu Dai Mountain. I immediately told him about that dream and asked if it could be believed? The Zen master said: "If the good heart is sincere and sincere, even doing one good deed can be equal to ten thousand good deeds. What's more, if you reduce taxes for an entire district, tens of thousands of people will enjoy that blessing." I immediately used my salary and sent the Zen Master to return to Wutai Mountain on my behalf to set up a ceremony to make offerings to ten thousand monks to dedicate their merits.

NOTE 1

Mr. Kong predicted that when I was 53 years old, I would have an accident [and die]. I never asked to live longer, but that year passed without anything happening. [When I wrote this chapter,] I was 69 years old.

The scriptures say: “Heaven's heart is hard to believe, fate is not certain.” It says: “Fate alone is not certain determined.” Those words are not false.

I understand from past events that everything Misfortunes and blessings are all self-inflicted. That is the teaching of the sages. If you think that misfortunes and blessings are predetermined by heaven, that is just the [deluded] words of secular people [who do not know how to practice].

What about when the network number is unknown? While your fortunes are glorious, you should often think that you are falling and falling; During times of good fortune, often imagine that you are encountering opposition and obstacles; While you are well-off and full, often think of yourself as being poor and hungry; While being respected by someone you love, often feel like you are afraid and worried; When you are in a high position of power, often think that you are in a lowly position; While you have a high and profound education, you should often think that you are a short-sighted and crude person.

If you think far, you often worry about upholding the virtues of your ancestors. If you think close, you often don't dare to expose your parents' mistakes and shortcomings. Above must always think about repaying the country's gratitude, below must always worry about creating happiness for the family; Always think about the outside world

When it comes to helping others when in need, you must always prevent your own evil thoughts. Every day [self-examination to] know your mistakes, every day you have to correct them; A day when you don't know your mistakes, that day you will still consider yourself right. A day where no mistakes are corrected is a day when there is no progress.

There are many intelligent and talented people in this world, but the reason they do not cultivate merit deeply and develop good karma widely is only because they are accustomed to following the old ways, are hesitant and timid, and are not determined enough to make efforts to change and establish their own destiny, so they continue to be infatuated throughout their lives.

The theory of "creating your own destiny" that Zen Master Van Coc taught is very effective. It is extremely profound and quintessential, indeed a very true and righteous principle. Anyone who can read these teachings carefully and try to follow them will not waste their life in vain.

tieu_de: Correct mistakes
noi_dung:
CORRECTING ERRORS

The officials of the Spring and Autumn period, when observing a person's behavior and words, often based on that to speculate about the good and bad things, misfortunes and misfortunes of that person, which always came true. Today, we can review these things in the books Ta Truyen, Quoc Ngu...

In general, omens of good things or disasters all arise from the human mind, then manifest on the outside in behavior and words. People who are extremely benevolent and generous and kind to others are often blessed, while those who are extremely strict and narrow-minded and mistreat others are often close to disaster. Ordinary people's physical eyes are heavily obscured [cannot see, so] they think that [fate] is not determined and cannot be predicted.

A person's heart that is extremely sincere is in accordance with the way of heaven. When blessings are about to come, you can know in advance by observing people's good deeds. When a disaster is about to happen, you can predict it by observing people's evil deeds. Now, if you want to receive blessings and avoid disasters, let's not talk about doing good deeds, but first worry about correcting mistakes.

When discussing correcting mistakes, the first important thing is to develop a sense of shame. Think of the sages from the past, how come they are human beings like us but can be teachers of eternity? And why have I been incompetent and useless like rubble and broken tiles all my life? It's just because we are infatuated with life's love, secretly do things that go against morality, and think that no one else knows, so we are calmly arrogant, without any shame, and one day fall into the beast world without even knowing it. There's really nothing greater than that in this life. Mencius said: "Knowing shame is an important virtue for humans. Keeping that mentality is a sage, if you lose it, you are no different from an animal." Therefore, starting

The mind of shame is the most essential foundation in correcting mistakes.

The next [important] thing is to know how to create a mind of fear [not daring to do something wrong]. Heaven and earth are seen from above, and ghosts and gods are not easily deceived. Now I'm doing something wrong, even though it's in a hidden place [no one can see it], but heaven and earth, demons and spirits can clearly see it. If it is a serious crime, it will surely bring down hundreds of thousands of disasters; If it is a light sin, it will certainly destroy existing merit and virtue; So how can one not be afraid?

Not only is it like that in a deserted place, but also in crowded places, even if we try to hide it very discreetly, explain very cleverly, but the things hidden in our hearts will soon be revealed, in the end we can't lie to ourselves. When others find out that they clearly know [the bad things they have done, then their own personality] is really not worth a penny! So how can you not be afraid?

Furthermore, as long as we have one breath left, no matter how great our sins are, we can repent. Once upon a time, there was a person who did evil deeds all his life. Only when he was about to die did he wake up and repent, generate a good thought, and immediately got good results. Therefore, it is said that starting a single very powerful good thought can counteract bad things for a hundred years. Just like a deep cave that has been dark for thousands of years, as soon as a light shines, the darkness of thousands of years is immediately destroyed. Therefore, regardless of whether mistakes were committed a long time ago or just recently, knowing how to correct them is the most valuable thing.

Life is impermanent, the human body is extremely fragile and easily lost. If one breath stops and does not continue, even if one wants to repent and correct, there will be no time left. At that time, on this earth, we will have to endure thousands of years of bad reputation. Even our good children and grandchildren will not be able to clean us up; In the realm of darkness, we will have to spend thousands of lifetimes in hell and endure karma. Even saints, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas cannot guide and save us. Oh, how can you not be afraid?

The third [important] thing is to develop a strong mind [to reform]. Most people in the world cannot correct their mistakes because they are so used to following the old ways that they fall into decline. We need to be excited and strong, not hesitant or stagnant, not procrastinating. For a small mistake, it should be considered as if a thorn punctured the flesh and should be quickly removed. For serious and serious errors, it must be considered as if the finger was bitten by a poisonous snake and immediately cut off without hesitation. That is talking about the benefits of [developing a strong mind, as fast as] lightning, like a strong wind.

Arising fully the 3 thoughts as above, [knowing shame, fear of mistakes and strong determination to correct] then every time you make a mistake you can immediately correct it. For example, if spring ice meets the sun, why not melt?

However, people's evil and evil mistakes can be corrected according to the manifestation of events, can also be corrected based on moral considerations, and can also be corrected right from the heart. Each such repair method requires different efforts, but the effectiveness is also different.

For example, in the past we used to kill lives, but now we keep the precept not to kill; Or like in the past, I was often angry, but now I try to control my anger. Such corrections are made according to the manifestation of things. Correcting in such a way means trying to suppress [the things that have manifested] on the outside, so it is extremely difficult, but the roots of those mistakes are still there in the end, except in one place, they will arise in another. This is not the ultimate way to completely correct all mistakes.

People who are more skillful in correcting mistakes will soon consider the morality of that event, when the incident has not yet manifested on the outside. For example, regarding the killing of life, immediately consider the morality: "Heaven and earth always have the virtue of love for life, all creatures are greedy for life and afraid of death. Now we kill animals to nourish our bodies, how can we feel at peace in our hearts? Moreover, the animal that was killed was stabbed and mutilated, then put into a pot of boiling water, a pan of hot oil, the pain and suffering penetrated to the marrow of the bones, we used its body to nourish ourselves, even if it was displayed into hundreds of bodies. Strange delicacies can be consumed once you eat them. Meanwhile, just a simple vegetable soup is enough to fill your stomach. Why must you kill the lives of all living beings and harm your own merit?"

Consider again that all creatures have flesh and blood and temperament, and also have spirituality and sentience. If we have spirituality and perception, then to [humans] we are the same being. Now that I myself have not been able to cultivate myself to become a supreme and virtuous being so that all living beings can respect and be close to me and rely on me, how can I still kill their lives, causing them to feel resentment and hatred towards me beyond words?

If you can thoroughly consider such things, when you see the food [that comes from killing] it must be extremely heartbreaking, impossible to swallow.

Or like before, when you are often angry, immediately consider: "For people who are not as good as us [behaving poorly], in terms of love, we should have compassion for them; for people who do unreasonable things [offend us], that is their wrong, what does it have to do with us?" Thinking like that, there's really nothing to be angry about.

Consider again that, in the world, there is no great man who complacently thinks he is right, nor is there any doctrine that teaches us to hate others. The virtues that have not been achieved are all due to our own merits and virtues that we have not cultivated properly and have not influenced others enough. We need to use those things to reflect and consider ourselves. So when someone comes to slander or humiliate you, you see it as rubbing and training [helping raw stones] become precious gems. As such, you must accept it with joy, how can you get angry?

Furthermore, if we are slandered and do not get angry, then those insults, no matter how many, are just like someone who lights a fire in the middle of nowhere, and will eventually extinguish on their own. If you hear slander and get angry, even if you wholeheartedly and skillfully defend yourself, it will be like a silkworm in spring that spins silk to make a cocoon, tying itself more and more tightly. Thus, anger is not only useless but also harmful.

For all other evil mistakes, the same is considered based on morality. If ethical considerations are clear and clear, all evil mistakes will end on their own.

What is correcting mistakes right from the heart? [That is self-examination], human mistakes and evils have countless causes, but they are all created by the mind. If our mind is peaceful and unmoved, then on what basis do mistakes arise? Practitioners who learn [this method of correcting errors] for evil mistakes such as lust, greed for fame, love of money, quick anger, etc. do not need to pursue and find remedies for each type. As long as they are single-mindedly focused on doing good, always maintaining the right thoughts, then many evil and evil thoughts will naturally not arise and cause pollution. For example, when the sun shines brightly in the sky, all kinds of demons and monsters hide. This is the most refined true transmission [error correction method]. All mistakes are created by the mind, so it is also up to the mind to correct them. For example, when cutting down poisonous trees, you have to cut them directly at the roots, there is no need to prune each branch and remove each leaf?

In general, the method of treating [mistakes] right from the heart is superior and most [effective]. While practicing to keep your mind pure, if [evil] thoughts start in your mind, you will immediately know it; Once you know clearly, [that evil] thought will naturally disappear.

If you do not have enough strength to practice according to the method of treating the mind, you should use the method of clear moral consideration to eliminate mistakes.

If you are still not strong enough to use the method of reasoning, you should use the method of treating according to the [wrong] thing that has been manifested.

If you use the highest method of treating the mind, along with the remaining methods, then there is nothing wrong. But if you only know how to use ineffective methods without knowing superior methods, it is foolish.

Therefore, when making a vow to correct bad mistakes, in a bright place you should pray for a good friend to remind you, in a dark place you should pray for a ghost or spirit to examine and prove it. Repent wholeheartedly for [past sins], day and night without any distractions, for a week, two weeks, up to a month, two months, three months... it must have a fulfilling effect. For example, feeling calm, relaxed and spacious; or feel like your mind is open, suddenly clear; Or there are times when you fall into a confusing situation but your emotions and thoughts are clear

no problems; Or there are times when you meet people who hate you but you can calm down and change your anger to be happy; or dream of vomiting dark objects; or dream of seeing the sages of the past appearing to guide and kindly guide you; or dreaming of yourself walking lightly in space, or dreaming of things like flags, precious parasols, all kinds of wonderful and wonderful scenes... All such things are manifestations of having eliminated evil and evil mistakes. However, we must not cling to such achievements and quickly develop an arrogant and complacent mind, because that will prevent us from making further progress.

Once upon a time, there was a person named Cu Ba Ngoc. When he was about 20 years old, he clearly saw his previous bad mistakes and was able to completely correct them. When I was 21 years old, I realized that my previous repentance had not actually ended [my mistakes]. At the age of 22, he looked back at the age of 21, [observed the past] as if in a dream, [continued to correct mistakes]. Just like that, year after year, he still persistently corrects errors. Even at the age of 50, you can still [look back] and see the mistakes you made at the age of 49.

Learning to correct errors is like that of the ancients. We are all ordinary mortals, with unspeakable accumulations of evil and mistakes, yet when we look back at past events, we often don't see any mistakes at all! It is because the mind is confused that the eyes are clouded.

However, when people's mistakes are too serious, there are visible signs. Not

such as having a gloomy, deadlocked spirit, saying something first and forgetting later, or without any reason but the mind is still often troubled and frustrated; Or when faced with a gentle and gentleman person, you feel ashamed and embarrassed; or hear righteous discussions but do not enjoy them; or often fall into the situation of doing favors and being resentful; or dreaming at night about crazy, contradictory things... If it's too serious, it can cause disordered speech and mental instability... All such things are manifestations of evil deeds. If you see one of these signs, you must immediately develop a strong and excited mind, determined to abandon old mistakes and build a new life.

I hope readers [understand the above correctly so] they don't deceive themselves.

tieu_de: Accumulate good things
noi_dung:
STORAGE OF GOOD THINGS

I Ching says: “A house that stores up good things will surely have an abundance of joy.” In the past, the Nhan family married their daughter to Thuc Luong Hot because they considered that his many ancestors had created many blessings. virtuous, therefore firmly believes that future descendants must be prosperous and good.1 Confucius, when praising King Shun as a man of great filial piety, said: “Ancestral temples are revered, many descendants to preserve the blessings.” Such words are all true

How is truth different from falsehood?

Once upon a time, there was a group of Confucian scholars who came to consult Venerable Trung Phong and asked: "Buddhism proposes the theory of cause and effect and retribution like a shadow following a shape, but now we see that person doing good deeds but their descendants do not prosper, and seeing that person doing evil deeds but their descendants are prosperous and prosperous. Thus, the Buddhist theory really has nothing to support."

The Venerable Trung Phong replied: "When feeling If worldly contact has not been completely eliminated, the true eyes cannot be opened. For good deeds, you see them as evil, and for evil deeds, you see them as good. Why do you not blame yourself for your mistakes in knowing the wrong way, but instead blame the karma of heaven for being wrong? class="book-paragraph">The monk immediately told them to each give a description to distinguish good from evil.

A person said: “Scolding and insulting others is evil; being respectful and polite to others is good.” Venerable Trung Phong said: "That is not necessarily the case."

Another person said: "Desire for money and doing wrong to take what belongs to others is evil; being honest and transparent and not defrauding and taking from others is good." Venerable Trung Phong said again: "That is not necessarily the case."

Each person in the group of Confucian students expressed their own understanding, but Venerable Trung Phong said it was not correct. Finally, the whole group asked him to give the correct reason.

The Venerable told them: "Doing things that benefit others is called good; doing things that only seek your own benefit is called evil. If it can bring benefits to others, then scolding and insulting others is also good. If it is only for your own personal benefit, being respectful and polite to others is also evil.

“ Therefore, If a person does good deeds for the benefit of others, then that common deed is true; Considering one's own interests as a private matter, that private [seeking of profit] must be a lie.

Once upon a time, King Shun was at the river wharf and saw

When he saw people who knew how to yield to others, he lavished praise and praise, and then did the same as that person. After King Shun did this for a year, everyone there gave each other the deep water and fish-rich areas.

[advice to others] is not effective, [on the contrary] you lose [relationship with] others, then you have to go back and examine your own intelligence [because you are not skillful enough].

5. What is saving people in times of danger?

Everyone in life has times of danger and trouble. If you encounter such situations, you should consider it as an emergency that is happening to you and must quickly rescue and rescue the situation. Or use words to help people clarify their injustice, or find all kinds of ways to help people in dire tribulation.

The Emperor said: “Grace is not precious in how much it is, but helping people in times of danger is important.” What a kind word indeed!

6. What is initiating and building things that are of great benefit to the community?

On a small scale, like in a village, on a larger scale, like in a district, if you see anything of common benefit, you should initiate and build it. These are things like digging water canals, building dikes to prevent floods, or repairing roads and bridges to make it easier for people on the road, or providing food and water to help people when they are hungry and thirsty... For those things, we should advise and encourage everyone to contribute together.

[Once done,] don't be afraid of others' suspicions, don't mind hardships.

7. What is spending money to work to create blessing?

Buddhist practice has thousands of good deeds, of which almsgiving is considered the foremost.1 When it comes to almsgiving, just one word of letting go is enough. Those who attain enlightenment let go of the six senses in their hearts, let go of the six senses on the outside,2 even all of their possessions, there is nothing that cannot be let go. People who have not yet reached that level must first let go of money and give it away as alms. People rely on food, clothing, and clothing to maintain their lives, so money is considered the most important thing. If we let go from that [most important] place, we can eliminate our own stinginess on the inside, and on the outside we can help other people's needs.

NOTE 1

Among the six paramitas of Bodhisattvas, the Paramitas of Generosity are also mentioned first: Generosity, Precepts, Patience, Diligence, Meditation and Wisdom.

NOTE 2

Six senses, including includes: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and mind. The six sense objects are the objects of the six senses, including: form, sound, smell, taste, touch and dharmas.

When you first start [doing alms], it often takes effort and force, but [with practice many times] it will eventually become liberal and natural. Giving alms is the best method to eliminate selfishness and eliminate attachment to greed.

8. What is supporting and protecting and preserving
Dharma?

Dharma is the bright eye that helps sentient beings forever be able to see [the path to escape suffering]. Without the Dharma, how can people [know how to obey] heaven and earth to contribute to survival? How can education and transformation be achieved for all species? How can we escape from all the delusion and bondage in worldly life? How can we enter this world to repair and improve our lives, and escape the cycle of birth and death?

Therefore, every time we encounter places where saints are worshiped or Dharma books are worshiped, we must revere and respect them, repair them, and decorate them beautifully. When it comes to upholding and widely spreading the Dharma and repaying the Buddha's gratitude, we must devote our wholehearted efforts.

9. What is respect for the elders,
?

Speaking of the elders, in the family there are parents, brothers and sisters, in the country there are officials, rulers, and in the whole society, all the elderly, virtuous people, people in superior positions or people with great knowledge, we Everyone should pay attention to respect and serve.

When serving your parents at home, you must be very respectful, have a cheerful appearance, and speak softly and gently. Getting used to this will become a naturally gentle personality, which is the basic element that can touch the heart of heaven.

When you step out into society to serve the country, no matter what you do, you must be careful yourself, not because your superiors don't know and do something wrong. If you are in a position to judge others, do not arbitrarily oppress others because your superiors do not know. There is an ancient saying: "Serving the country is like worshiping heaven and earth." Those are places closely related to [human] sound virtue. Just look at the families of those who maintain loyalty and filial piety, and you will clearly see that there is no family that does not have long-lasting, prosperous descendants. So it is necessary to be careful with this.

10. What is knowing how to respect life,
love and regret the lives of all
species?

Humans deserve to be called human only by having compassion. To have kindness, you must first have compassion; If you want to accumulate merit, you must first accumulate compassion. The Book of Zhou Rites says: “During the spring month, sacrifices must not use female animals.”1 Mencius said: “A gentleman stays away

NOTE 1

Because most animals are in their breeding season in the spring month, I'm afraid that using female animals for sacrifice will kill the fetus in her womb.

the kitchen.”1 Things like that are all to preserve compassion and [know how to mourn for life]. Therefore, the ancients had four types of meat to avoid eating. They are: (1) meat from animals that scream when being killed, (2) meat from animals that are seen when being killed, (3) meat from animals that they raise themselves, (4) meat from animals that others intentionally kill for their own enjoyment. see.

If religious students cannot completely stop eating meat, they should start by avoiding eating the above types of meat, gradually improving, their compassion is nurtured and stronger, then not only can they keep the precept of not killing, but [can also deeply realize that] all insects, insects, animals... have life and need to be respected. Things like boiling silkworm cocoons to spin silk, plowing the land to kill insects... are all killing, and our food and clothes come from such things, so it is no different from killing other species to gain life for ourselves. Understanding this, we can see that the waste of food, supplies... is no different from the crime of murder. As for things like accidentally killing or trampling on [insects], it's impossible to know how many there are, so we have to be very careful and limit them. There is an ancient saying:

Save leftover grains of rice, pity hungry mice,
Keep your life and burn yourself, don't light a lamp.2

NOTE 2

These two lines of poetry by the great poet To Dong Pha, the original Chinese text is: 愛鼠常留飯，憐蛾不點燈 - (Love is always saved in the Sanskrit, is not the point of posting.) The main idea is that, because of pity for hungry rats, when they eat, they leave some leftover rice behind without cleaning it up; Because I don't want the moths to die by jumping into the fire, I don't light the lamp.

How benevolent!

*>

There are so many virtuous actions that it is impossible to list them all, but from the ten things just mentioned above, if considered broadly, thousands of merits can all be complete.

tieu_de: Maintain humility
noi_dung:
KEEP HUMILITY

The I Ching says: “The way of heaven often eliminates the excess and makes up for the lack; the way of the earth often changes the fullness and leaves the lack intact; demons and spirits often harm the abundant place but bless the humble place; human hearts often hate arrogant people but loves humble people.”

[Heaven, earth, ghosts and humans all love humility,] that's why [in the I Ching] just one Humble hexagram means all 6 lines are good.

The scriptures say: “Prosperity often brings harm, humility brings benefits.”

I have taken the exam many times with other people, every time When meeting a poor student who is about to pass the exam, we all see a humble appearance clearly visible on the outside.

In the year of the Goat, 1 among the bachelors who returned to the capital to take the exam, our group of Gia Thien compatriots had

NOTE 1

That is in 1571. In this exam, Vien Lieu Pham did not take the exam. pass.

10 people. Dinh Kinh Vu is the youngest person, with a very humble personality. I told Phi Cam Pha: "This guy will definitely pass the exam this year."

The Phi family asked again: "How do we know?"

I replied: "Only humble people can receive blessings. Do you think there is anyone among us who is honest and simple, tolerant and does not fight like Kinh Vu? Is there anyone who is respectful and obedient, completely humble like Kinh Vu? Is there anyone who is oppressed by people without needing to respond, who is criticized by people without needing to justify like Kinh Vu? If someone is like that, heaven, earth, ghosts and spirits will always help, how can they not rise up? okay?”

When the board was posted, Kinh Vu was indeed accepted.

In the year of Dinh Suu1 I returned to the capital, lived in the same place with Phung Khai Chi, and found that this man had a humble personality and solemn appearance, largely because he had been accustomed to it since childhood. At that time, Ly Te Nham was a good friend, with a straightforward personality. He often publicly criticized Khai Chi's mistakes. I only saw him calmly listen and accept, never having a word of objection. At that time, I told Khai Chi: "All blessings have a root cause, and disasters also have a previous origin. If your heart is truly humble, God will help you. This year you will definitely pass the exam." Indeed, that is true.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1577.

Mr. Trieu Du Phong, named Quang Vien, was a man

Guan district in Shandong province. At a young age, he passed the bachelor's exam in Huong exam, but after a long time [took the Hoi exam many times] he did not pass. His father was appointed as the Chief of Staff in Gia Thien district, and he followed his father to take office. Because he admired Tien Minh Ngo's writing, he brought his essay to the Tien family to see. Tien Minh Ngo took a look and immediately lost all the cards. Not only was Trieu Du Phong not angry, he was also full of admiration and quickly corrected himself. The following year, he immediately passed the exam.

In the year of the Dragon,2 I went to the capital to meet the court, and at that time I met Ha Kien So. I see that this man has a calm demeanor and is not complacent, his mind is humble, and his humility is clearly visible to everyone. When returning home, I told my friends: "Usually when heaven is about to help someone prosper, before blessing him, he will first make that person develop wisdom. Once wisdom arises, people who are deceitful and playful will become sincere and faithful, people who are careless and careless will know how to control and restrain themselves. Mr. Kien So is gentle and gentle like that, it means that God has opened up [wisdom], [he will surely be granted it tomorrow]. Phuc].”

NOTE 2

That is the year 1592.

By the time the board was posted, Ha Kien So indeed passed the exam.

Truong Uy Nham was from Giang Am district, learned a lot, and had a reputation in the literary world. Go to

in the year of Giap Ngo,1 he returned to Nanjing to take the Perfume exam, staying in a temple. When the exam results were posted and he did not see his name accepted, he cursed the examiner, saying he had no eyes. At that time, a Taoist monk standing nearby burst out laughing. The Truong family immediately turned angry at the Taoist priest.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1594.

The Taoist said: “Your writing is definitely not good.”

The Truong family became even angrier and shouted: "You've never read my writing, how do you know it's not good?"

The Taoist said: "I heard that writers are most precious because of their peaceful and calm temperament. Now, listening to you scolding, [if the temperament] doesn't have any peace and quiet at all, how can the writing be good?"

The Truong family name Hearing that, I suddenly admired him and immediately bowed and asked for instructions. The Taoist said: "Whether you pass the exam or not depends on your fate. If your fate is not worthy of passing, even if you write well, it is of no use. You should change yourself."

Truong Uy Nham from then on followed the teachings, tried to correct himself, abandoned his arrogance and maintained humility, his good heart grew more and more, his virtue became deeper and deeper. In the year of the Rooster,1 he dreamed of going to an upper room, seeing a book recording the names of people who passed the exam, many of which were empty rows, and immediately asked a person standing next to him: "The list of names of people who passed the exam is missing, why are there so many names missing?" That person replied: "When selecting people to pass, in the underworld, every 3 years, there will be a comparison review. NOTE 1

That is the year 1597.

In the exam that year Truong Uy Nham indeed passed and ranked. 105th.2

So this man entered the Tam Giac rank, that is, Dong Doctors came from, because in the Ming Dynasty, only the Tam Giac rank had up to 130 people.

Due to the above things, we know that, above the three meters1, there must be divine scrutiny. Good and bad things, good and bad, are definitely up to you. You need to know how to maintain a good heart, control all your actions, not commit the slightest bit of evil, always be humble and humble, so that heaven, earth, ghosts and gods will be moved to help, only then can you have the foundation to enjoy blessings. A person who has an arrogant and complacent temperament must be short-sighted, and even if he has prosperity and development, he cannot enjoy it [for a long time]. No one with a little knowledge and understanding would be willing to fall into such a narrow tolerance and lose their blessings. What's more, humility opens up the opportunity to learn from others, and to be able to accept and imitate other people's good deeds, without limits.

NOTE 1

The original text uses tam chi (三尺), which means 3 ancient meters, equal to about 1 meter. However, in this idiom, this is just a symbolic number.

A person who seeks a successful career cannot lack humility. There is an old saying: "If you have the will to become famous, you will surely gain fame; if you have the will to become rich, you will surely get rich." A person with ambition is like a tree with roots. If you want to establish a strong reputation for success, you must always maintain a humble heart and skillfully use countless means [to do good deeds], and naturally you will be moved by heaven and earth. Therefore, merit and virtue are all created by ourselves.

People today want to pass exams, but at first they often do not have a true ambition, it is just

it is just temporary excitement. When you're excited, you'll wish for it. When you're no longer excited, you'll stop wishing for it. Mencius said [to the king of Qi]: "The king loves music very much, the state of Qi is about to prosper."1 I am the same with the academic career path.2

NOTE 1

In this dialogue, Mencius linked the king's love of music to the rule of the country and stated the main principle: If the king enjoys listening to music that can make all the people rejoice with him, the country will be prosperous.

Mr. Vien Lieu Pham's idea here is that when we seek fame and career, we must also know how to aim for the common good in the community, trying to do good and accumulate virtue is to benefit many people. If you do that, you will achieve your desire and make many others happy.
